* VIP Compile Options
Most VIPs support a set of compile-time options and macro constants which control
various features of the VIP. These are applied during the compile phase using the
+define+<option>=<value> syntax. Values which are supplied in this section are
checked to validate that the option provided are recognized by the VIP.
; Set a VIP compile-time option
[VIP_DEFINES]
UVM_DISABLE_AUTO_ITEM_RECORDING = 1

UVM_PACKER_MAX_BYTES = 1500000
SVT_AXI_MAX_ADDR_WIDTH = 32

* Compile Directives
General compile-time options can be provided in this section. Each value is applied
as-is on the compile command. This section is not name/value pairs like the other
sections. No checking is performed on these values.
; Set a general compile-time option
[COMPILE_DIRECTIVES]
-kdb=common_elab
-quiet
+define+ENABLE_DUT_DEBUG=1

* Elaboration Directives
General elaboration-time options can be provided in this section. Each value is applied
as-is on the elaboration command. This section is not name/value pairs like the other
sections. Checking is not performed on these values.
; Set a general elaboration-time option
[ELABORATION_DIRECTIVES]
-debug_access+pp
-P pli.tab
msglog.o

* Runtime Directives
General run-time options can be provided in this section. Each value is applied as-is on
the elaboration command. This section is not name/value pairs like the other sections.
Checking is not performed on these values.
; Set a general run-time option
[RUNTIME_DIRECTIVES]
-cm line

* Ad Hoc Signal Declaration
There may be a need to declare ad hoc signals in the DUT wrapper. The following INI
section can be used to declare a single signal.
[SIGNALS]
name = ad_hoc_signal0
type = bit
value = 1'b0

The name and type entries are required. The value entry is optional, if it is not provided
then the signal is declared and not initialized to any value. For example, the entry
above results in the following signal declaration in the dut_wrapper:
bit ad_hoc_signal0 = 1'b0;

The following is the entry:
[SIGNALS]
name = ad_hoc_signal1
type = logic [3:0]

This results in the following signal being declared:
logic [3:0] ad_hoc_signal1;

* VIP Signal Connection Override
The tool attempts to automatically connect VIP signals to DUT signals. There may be
some situations where you want to override the automated connections. The following
INI section can be used to achieve overrides for VIP signal connections:
[VIP_SIGNAL_CONNECTION_OVERRIDE]
name = ahb_if_0.slave_if[0].hsel
value = ad_hoc_signal0

The value provided to the 'name' entry should be the hierarchical path to the VIP
interface signal to be assigned. The hierarchical path should begin with the VIP
interface instance. Since the instance name of this interface is not known when the tool
is first invoked, these connections likely need to be declared in the INI file used by a
second invocation of the tool.
The value provided to the 'value' entry could be an ad hoc signal that was previously
declared, or it could be a constant value. The tool uses the value that is provided as a
string.
* DUT Signal Connection Override
The tool attempts to automatically connect VIP signals to DUT signals. There may be
some situations where you want to override the automated connections. The following
INI section can be used to achieve overrides of DUT signal connections:
[DUT_SIGNAL_CONNECTION_OVERRIDE]
name = Structure_inst.CPU1_HSel
value = ad_hoc_signal0

The value provided to the 'name' entry should be the hierarchical path to the DUT port
to be assigned. The hierarchical path should begin with the DUT instance. Since the
name of this instance is not known when the tool is first invoked, these connections
need to be declared in the INI file used by a second invocation of the tool.
The value provided to the 'value' entry can be an ad hoc signal that was previously
declared, or it can be a constant value. The tool uses the value that is provided as a
string.
* DUT Parameter Override

The tool attempts to populate DUT parameters with default values from DUT IP-XACT
file. However, the default value in the DUT IP-XACT file may not match actual value in the
DUT file. The following INI section can be used to override a DUT parameter value:
[DUT_PARAMETER_OVERRIDE]
name = cci400_inst.AWUSER_WIDTH
value = 2

The value provided to the 'name' entry should be the hierarchical path to the DUT
parameter to be assigned. The hierarchical path should begin with the DUT instance.
Since the name of this instance is not known when the tool is first invoked, these
connections need to be declared in the INI file used by a second invocation of the tool.
The value provided to the 'value' entry is a constant value. The tool uses the value that is
provided as a string.
* DUT Files
The DUT IP-XACT may contain information about how to load the DUT, but the
information is optional and therefore this information may not be present. The following
INI section can be provided which causes the dut_files file to be populated with the
provided values:
[DUT_FILES]
path_to_dut_file1
path_to_dut_file2
17.18UVM REG

To support UVM REG, the tool assumes that you have already run ralgen and
generated the uvm_reg_block extension for their DUT. The name of the file that
contains the register model and the name of the model itself must be provided through
the INI file.
[UVM_REG]
file = ral_MemoryMap_MCU.sv
model = ral_sys_MemoryMap_MCU
ralgen_options = -uvm -t MemoryMap_MCU dut.ralf
enabled = true

* Internal Clock/Reset
The tool creates clock/reset generators in the testbench top. However, the clock/reset
source can be already in the DUT. These INI sections provide a method to use an
internal clock/reset.
[INTERNAL_CLOCK]
name = ex_aclk
source =
Subsytem_cci500_tbclkgen_internal_inst.i_TB_clkgen.aclk
is_default = true
[INTERNAL_RESET]

name = ex_aresetn
source = Subsytem_cci500_tbclkgen_internal_inst.i_TB_clkgen.aresetn
is_default = true

* FILESET Setting
The file set provides the file list for simulation. You can select a different file list by
specifying the name of an IP-XACT view. This INI section provides a method to change
the root and the view of the file set.
[SET_FILESET]
instance = top_inst
view = RTL
root = ./src

* User Extensions
User extensions allow you to add additional capabilities to the generated testbench.
This INI section provides a method to describe the prefix used and the location of these
extensions.
[USER_EXTENSIONS]
prefix = project_prefix
env_dir = /remote/project/tb_env_ext
tests_dir = /remote/project/tb_test_ext

* PHY_CONNECTION
If the DUT exposes the parallel interface of a PHY, then the DUT Connection section
allows you to select whether the generated testbench should include a PHY Shell
Module or if the testbench should instead connect the VIP directly to the parallel
interface (if the VIP supports this). The busdefs are identified using the VLNV, and if
any of the settings are not specified, then it is treated as a wildcard situation for that
setting.
To set up for a specific bus type identified by VLNV:
[PHY_CONNECTION]
parallel_busdef_vendor = synopsys.com
parallel_busdef_library = busdef.phy
parallel_busdef_name = pipeV4
parallel_busdef_version = 4.1
serial_busdef_vendor = synopsys.com
serial_busdef_library = busdef.phy
serial_busdef_name = pcie-txrx-phy
serial_busdef_version = 2.0
direct_connect = [0|1]

To set up for a specific bus instance:
[PHY_CONNECTION]
dut_bus_name = ddr4_dfi_if_inst.DWC_ddr_umctl2_dfi

serial_busdef_vendor = synopsys.com
serial_busdef_library = busdef.phy
serial_busdef_name = pcie-txrx-phy
serial_busdef_version = 2.0
direct_connect = [0|1]

* COMPONENT_CONTROL_OPTIONS
You can select the control options in this section. Each section instance defines
settings that are to be applied to an individual component or component view. To
differentiate controls associated with different component versions, the component is
represented by its VLNV value. If any of the VLNV settings is not specified, then it is
treated as a wildcard situation for that setting. If the view value is not specified, then the
settings are applied to all of the component's views.
[COMPONENT_CONTROL_OPTIONS]
vendor = arm.com
library = Cores
name = CORTEX15
version = r4p1_0
view = verilog
use_file_list = [0|1]
use_y = [0|1]
add_file_based_incdir = [0|1]
add_includes_to_file_list = [0|1]
add_synopsys_sim_ver = [0|1]
add_v2k = [0|1]
add_vhdl87 = [0|1]

* DUT_PARAMETER_OVERRIDE
VC AutoTestbench attempts to populate DUT parameters with the default value from
DUT IP-XACT file. However, the default value in the DUT IP-XACT file may not match
the actual value in the DUT file.
The following INI section can be used to specify overrides for the DUT parameter
value:
[DUT_PARAMETER_OVERRIDE]
name = cci400_inst.AWUSER_WIDTH
value = 2

The value provided to the name entry should be the hierarchical path to the DUT
parameter to be assigned. The hierarchical path should begin with the DUT instance.
Since the instance name of this instance is not known when the tool is first invoked,
these connections likely need to be declared in the INI file used by a second invocation
of the tool.
The value provided to the value entry is a constant value. The template uses the value
that is provided as a string.

* TESTBENCH_TOP
In case you want to use your own DUT wrapper instead of using the one generated by
the tool, you must specify the module name of the provided wrapper and the full path of
the DUT inside the wrapper module.
[TESTBENCH_TOP]
module = testbench_top
dut_path = user_dut_inst

* VIP Version
The latest version of the VIPs in the DESIGNWARE_HOME directory (and the directories
specified using the VC_VCATB_CUSTOM_VIP_PATH environment variable) are scanned
by the tool for possible VIP matches.

You can indicate that unmatched DUT VLNV signatures can be ignored using the
following section in the INI file.

ignore = 1

Support for DUT Parameters (Batch Mode)
VC AutoTestbench populates DUT parameters with the default value from the DUT IPXACT file. However, the default value in the DUT IP-XACT file may not match the actual
value in the DUT file.
To override the DUT parameter values, add the [DUT_PARAMETER_OVERRIDE] section in
the config.ini file.
[DUT_PARAMETER_OVERRIDE]
name = cci400_inst.AWUSER_WIDTH

The value provided to the name entry is the hierarchical path of the DUT parameter to be
assigned. The hierarchical path must begin with the DUT instance. Since the instance
name of this instance is not known when the tool is initially invoked, these connections
need to be declared in the .ini file used when the tool is invoked later.
The value provided to the value entry is a constant value. The template uses the value
that is provided as a string.

Component Fileset Settings (Batch Mode)
VC AutoTestbench provides you the component fileset setting to specify more information
to build a component.
You can define settings for an individual component or a component view in the
[COMPONENT_CONTROL_OPTIONS] section of the config.ini file.
To differentiate controls associated with different component versions, the component is
represented by its VLNV value. If any of the VLNV settings are not specified, it is treated
as a wildcard situation for that setting. If the view value is not specified, then the settings
are applied to all of views of the component.
An example of the [COMPONENT_CONTROL_OPTIONS] section, where, 0 corresponds to
disabling the option and 1 corresponds to enabling the option:
[COMPONENT_CONTROL_OPTIONS]
vendor = arm.com
library = Cores

view = verilog
use_file_list = [0|1]
use_y = [0|1]
add_file_based_incdir = [0|1]
add_includes_to_file_list = [0|1]
add_synopsys_sim_ver = [0|1]
add_v2k = [0|1]
add_vhdl87 = [0|1]

component or component view in the [COMPONENT_COMPILE_DIRECTIVES] section. Each
value is applied to the per view file lists that are generated. If view value is not specified,
the settings are applied to all component views. No checking is performed on these
values.

If you want to use your own DUT wrapper instead of using the one generated by the tool,
you need to specify the module name of the provided wrapper and the full path of the DUT

If the DUT exposes the parallel interface of a PHY, you can select whether the generated
testbench must include a PHY shell module or the testbench should connect the VIP

Support for Verdi Machine Learning Library
Starting with this release, Verdi provides you an unified platform to collect data from EDA
tools and allows you to access data for machine learning applications. This platform
includes three abstract layers, such as table, model, and application.Each layer can read
and write from the database of APIs.
In the table layer, the tables are constructed using both C++ and Python. In this layer, you
can construct your own tables and extract specific data by any utility. You can also read
these tables using Python.
In the model layer, pre-defined types and properties can be selected to extract data from
the database by different utilities. These tables can be read using Python as well where
pre-defined relations between types are resolved. Currently, only 'waveform' model is
In the application layer, both the data collection and access methods are provided in the
'Database' class of the 'verdilearn' package in Python. You can take the tables as an input
to their machine learning applications.
These tables provide information about the C++ and Python APIs.

Siloti What-if
The following section describes the Siloti What-if LCA feature supported by Verdi as part
of this release:
* WISIM Replay Block Stimuli on SoC
* Assertion Replay for Emulation/FPGA Prototyping

WISIM Replay Block Stimuli on SoC
All the ports are dumped to the FSDB file in a block-level simulation with block-level
testbench. Then, the captured block-level stimuli are applied on the SoC simulation
environment. During the SoC simulation, the block inputs are overwritten by the captured
block-level stimuli. At last, the two FSDB files dumping from block and SoC simulations
are compared. You can specify the stimuli and compare mapping files or it can be
generated automatically.
Figure 409

Use Model of WISIM Replay Block Stimuli on SoC

The concept of time-frame is depicted in the following figure. You can specify the time
range (Begin_Time and End_Time) for replay simulation and applying FSDB stimuli. While

WISIM Replay Block Stimuli on SoC

running the simulation with WISIM Testbench until Begin_Time (replay), block-level stimuli
from Begin_Time (stimuli) is applied to the SoC-TB. In other words, the FSDB stimuli are
shifted. After the maximum time of FSDB stimuli, the Replay simulation may continue
running until End_Time (replay).
Figure 410

Depiction of Time-range

Required Data
For the block stimuli replay flow, a few additional files and settings must be prepared and
specified. After running the simulation, some additional files are generated. The complete
configuration is described below.
The following files must be prepared, if needed, depending on whether you use the twostep or three-step flow in VCS:
* The FSDB file dumping form block-level testbench (BL-TB) simulation, for example,
block.fsdb

* The run file of SoC testbench (SoC-TB) simulation (for VCS two-step flow), for
example, run_soc.f
* The configurations for replay simulation, for example, wi_config
* The simulation compile script, for example, wi_compile.rc
* The simulation run script, for example, wi_run.rc
* The VCS configuration (for VCS three-step flow), for example, synopsys_sim.setup
The following mapping files need to be manually prepared, or they are automatically
created by specific configurations:
* The mapping of input stimuli to apply to the Replay Simulation, for example,
stimuli.map

* The mapping of signals to apply waveform comparison, for example, compare.map

WISIM Replay Block Stimuli on SoC

The following resultant output files are generated.
* The FSDB file by Replay simulation on the SoC after applying the block stimuli, for
example, wi_result.fsdb
* The comparison error report between BL-TB and SoC-TB simulations, for example,
wi_cmp_error.nce

* The comparison summary between BL-TB and SoC-TB simulations in wi_flow.log
To use WISIM to replay block stimuli on SoC, perform the following steps:
* Preparation (for VCS three-step flow):
Analyze the SoC design using vlogan and vhdlan for SystemVerilog and VHDL design,
respectively, and prepare the corresponding script for the analyzed library. Prepare the
configuration file and the corresponding scripts.
* Extract:
Generate WISIM testbench using the -replay_extract option. With Auto_Map and
Auto_Compare_Map, the automatic mapping files are generated in this phase. When
the mapping files or configuration are modified, you can add the -remap option after
-replay_extract to run the remap flow. You can skip generating the design by setting
the environment variable WISIM_SKIP_CG to 1, if you use VCS three-step flow. Then,
load designs from library (analyzed with -kdb=common_elab) with -lib options with
-replay_extract.
* Compile:
Compile the SoC design and WISIM testbench, using the -replay_compile option.
If you compile in the SoC environment, add wi_test.sv during compilation (two-step
flow) or analyze wi_test.sv into witbLib and add WI_TB_TOP (three-step flow) during
elaboration in compile script.
* Simulate:
Run simulation for the SoC design by applying FSDB stimuli under WISIM
testbench, using the -replay_sim option. With Compare_Map or Auto_Compare_Map,
wi_result.fsdb is automatically compared with the block-level one. It is able to
re-compare the same FSDB files with different options (Compare_Option) or signal
mapping (Compare_Map and Auto_Compare_Map) by adding the -recompare option
after -replay_sim.

PureLog Interface
PureLog includes three types of windows:
* SmartLog: The SmartLog window is mainly used to navigate certain log and is opened
by default with the binary PureLog. You can also open a new SmartLog window
through the SmartLog menu (Tools > New SmartLog) or the SmartSheet menu (Tools
> New SmartSheet).
* SmartSheet: The SmartSheet window is mainly used to navigate PureLog DB and is
opened by default with the binary PureLogDB. You can also open a new SmartSheet
window through the SmartLog menu (Tools > SmartSheet).
* nWave: The nWave window is used to visualize log messages through query
conditions that can help you comprehend log messages efficiently.

The SmartLog engine can be used to read and traverse log files in a readable view.
SmartLog loads a log file with a specific format that shows a structured presentation of the
log contents, thus providing a flexible and convenient use model for debugging.

The connection between the log file and the Verdi platform is built according to the
hyperlink rule files and the partitioning rule files.
For more information about SmartLog, refer to the SmartLog Tutorial chapter of Verdi User
Guide and Tutorial.
In addition to the classical functions, PureLog adds many advanced features to SmartLog.

Traverse Related Message Search Mechanism
PureLog traces 1000 blocks upward or downward from the starting block that you rightclick. A block is a group of messages with the first line matched by the partitioning rule, for
example, UVM header.
PureLog analyzes the first three lines of each block because:
* The key-value attributes are most likely to sit in the first few lines.
* It can speed up the searching.
Key and value are matched by the exact match mode by default.

When debugging the log, you may want to compare the error log with the golden log to
see the differences. However, sometimes there are a lot of differences at a certain point
that make it hard to get clues from it.
Figure 469

Compare Error Log With Golden Log

The general solution is to dump the waveform, but it requires rerunning the simulation that
takes a lot of time. In addition, the design verification engineers might not know a design
very well and may put in extra efforts to pick signals from the design under test (DUT).
PureLog provides a way to dump the waveform from the log directly. The advantage of this
feature is that you do not need to rerun the simulation and also do not need to pick signals
from the DUT. You only need to know the log well. In the log, you can show messages
about interface connection, such as UART transaction, Ethernet Tx/Rx transactions, and
so on. You can pick some of them and dump to the waveform for observation.

Signal Type of Log-to-Wave
The following are the rules for log-to-wave to determine a signal type:
* Contains only a positive integer or a value string (for example, 0x123) : bit-vector
(digital)
* Contains a floating point number or a non-positive integer : analog
* Contains non-numerical data : enum

The PureLog DB enables you to keep the information of logs through the logCompile
script. Whenever you need to check a log for debugging, you can access it through APIs
or by using the simple UI query system. Some PureLog features also rely on the PureLog
DB. Generally, the PureLog DB can be written by the daily regression script at night and
can be accessed by you or PureLog in daytime.

Benefits of PureLog DB
The PureLog DB has the following benefits:
* Better performance: Most PureLog features can have better performance with the
PureLog DB.
* Less memory consumption: Most PureLog features can have less memory
consumption with the PureLog DB.
* AI technology: AI-related features of PureLog rely on the PureLog database.
* Customized application: You can access the PureLog DB through APIs or by using the
query system UI. Based on APIs and query systems, it is easy to develop a customized
application. It means that you can have your own debugging way.

Overall Flow in Simulation Application
Figure 480

Flow in Simulation Application

Setting Up the PureLog DB Server
Before saving or reading logs from the PureLog DB, you need to launch the server.
PureLog provides the msgdbControl utility to start or stop the server.

Starting the Server
Run the following command:
msgdbControl -start_server -storage_path <database storage path>

After starting the server, you can compile logs by logCompile and debug on DB debug
platform.

Stopping the Server
Run the following command:
msgdbControl -stop_server -storage_path <database storage path>

Remember to stop server:
* When you finish debugging.
* Before you want to clean up the DB storage.

Restarting the Server
You can restart the server under the same DB storage path. The compiled logs are
preserved.
msgdbControl -stop_server -storage_path <database storage path>

%> msgdbControl -start_server -storage_path <database storage path>
%> logCompile <opts> # compile/debug
%> msgdbControl -stop_server -storage_path <database storage path>
%> msgdbControl -start_server -storage_path <database storage path> #
restart server

Compiling Logs Into the PureLog DB
PureLog provides the logCompile utility to compile log information into the PureLog DB.
The utility supports CSV format and customized format.

CSV Format
(-log_type="csv")
logCompile
[-log_type="csv"]
-storage_path="<database_storage_path>"
-project_name="<project_name>"
-log_list="<log.ls>"
-separator=','
[-comment='#']
[-none_regexp='-+']
[-quotechar='"']
[-escapechar="\"]
[-hyper_rule="<hyper_rule_path>"]
[-date ="date"]

In case of CSV format, logCompile removes leading and trailing whitespace for each cell
and skips a blank line.
The CSV file list is specified in -log_list="<log.ls>".In this input file, each line includes
two sections. The left side is the input file path, and the right side is the database file path
to be saved.
Example log.ls file
./trace1.csv user_case/trace1.log
./trace2.csv user_case/trace2.log
./trace3.csv user_case/trace3.log

Customized Format
(-log_type="user_defined")
logCompile
[-log_type="user_defined"]
-storage_path="<database_storage_path>"
-project_name="<project_name>"
-log_list="<log.ls>"
-attr_rule_list="<rule.ls>"
[-hyper_rule="<hyper_rule_path>"]
[-date="date"]

For customized logs, logCompile requires the -attr_rule_list option whose input is
the list of SmartLog partition rules. All features extracted from partition rules are saved into
the PureLog DB. It is recommended to use the SmartLog UI to develop partition rules first
to ensure that all features are extracted correctly.
Example rule.ls file
attr_rule_general.rc
attr_rule_dramc.rc
attr_rule_mcard.rc

The file list is specified in -log_list="<log.ls>". In this input file, each line includes two
sections. The left side is the input file path, and the right side is the database file path to
be saved.
Example log.ls file
./sim_all.log proj/case1/sim_all.log
./sim_dramc.log proj/case1/sim_dramc.log
./sim_mcardlog proj/case1/sim_mcard.log

simWLogCompile
simWLogCompile is a wrapper that enables you to run simulation and compile the
generated simulation log with logCompile simultaneously. This approach helps to reduce

the time required to generate the Log Database.

Wrapper Options
All the options that contain %> simWLogCompile -h except -virtual_path and
-central_storage_path are passed to logCompile.

The simWLogCompile wrapper is used to execute simulation and compile logs
simultaneously through the following steps:
1. Use msgdbControl to start the local Log Database server at the beginning and stop it
at the end.
2. Collect and remove the options which are used by logCompile.
3. Start local DB server.
4. Launch VCS or simv with remaining options.
5. Launch logCompile with collected options to compile target log specified by the -l
option or -incr_log option.
Ctrl+C kills VCS or simv and logCompile.
6. Stop the local DB server when both the simulation and logCompile is completed.
The following specifies the options for the simWLogCompile wrapper:
Must Have Option for Wrapper
* -incr_log <TARGET_LOG> : Specify the log to be generated by the simulation and
compiled by logCompile. This option does NOT pass to the simulation.
* -l <TARGET_LOG> : Specify the log to be generated by the simulation and compiled by
logCompile. This option passes to the simulation.
When both -l and -incr_log are present simultaneously, the value of
-incr_log is prioritized.
Primary Options for Wrapper
The primary options for wrapper are optional.
* -storage_path <STORAGE_PATH>:
Path to local storage path.
Default: ./simWLogCompileDir/db_storage
* -project_name <DB_NAME>:
Database name.
Default: defaultProjectName

* -virtual_path <VIRTUAL_PATH>:
Specify the virtual path to be stored in the database.
Default: simWLogCompileDir/<TARGET_LOG>

<TARGET_LOG> is specified by -l or -incr_log option.

* -num_process <NUM_WORKS>: Number of logCompile worker processes for parallel
compilation.
Default: 1

Types of Simulation
The simWLogCompile wrapper consists of following types of simulation:
One Step Simulation
* %> simWLogCompile vcs -debug_access+all -lca -sverilog

-ntb_opts uvm-1.1 -timescale=1ns/100ps +incdir+$SVTB_PATH
+incdir+$RTL_PATH $DUT_LOAD -R +UVM_VERBOSITY=UVM_MEDIUM
+UVM_TESTNAME=test_r8_w8_r4_w4 +ntb_random_seed=1 +UVM_NO_RELNOTES
+FSDB_ON +UVM_TR_RECORD +UVM_LOG_RECORD +fsdbfile+verdi_i.fsdb
+UVM_VERDI_TRACE="UVM_AWARE|RAL|TLM|MSG|HIER|PRINT" -l

Attributes in the PureLog DB
The attributes can be kept in the PureLog DB as string type or numeral type. You can
impose only numeral query on numeral attributes through APIs or the DB debug platform.
If you expect the attributes to be saved in numeral type, here is the summary of the
supported format:
* Number with decimal point (example, 1.6)
* Verilog integer literal constants (size <= 64)
* 0x (example, 0x1200)

VC AutoTestbench
Verdi provides the VC AutoTestbench tool for testbench generation using the information
extracted from DUT IP-XACT file, VIP IP-XACT files and other configuration files provided
by users. VC AutoTestbench allows you to customize various aspects of a testbench,
such as, topology, interface and signal-level connections, clock or reset connection, and
so on. This tool enables easy and rapid generation of a testbench, which is usually a
time consuming and an error-prone process and it gates the actual testing for simulation,
acceleration, or emulation.

The VC AutoTestbench tool uses a licensing mechanism that is enabled by the
following license switches: VC-AUTO-TESTBENCH-VERDI-PLUGIN VC-AUTOTESTBENCH

Prerequisites

This chapter contains the following sections that provide details about VC AutoTestbench:

Prerequisites
The following are the prerequisites for using the VC AutoTestbench tool:
* AMBA-specific Protocol IP-XACT files are included in the Verdi installation under the
FOSS agreement. You also need to download ARM.COM IPXACT/busdefs. Get them
from the Corelink Creator or from the ARM IP areas.
* You need to extract DUT IP-XACT files along with RTL/Verilog files. Extract them from
Synopsys Core Tools (coreConsultant and coreAssembler), ARM Tools (coreLink
Creator andAMBA Designer), Arteris FLexNoC tool, or other SoC Assembly tools.
These IPXACT files use the IEEE-1685-2009 format.
* You must set the environment variables as follows:
setenv VCS_HOME <VCS_INST_DIR>
setenv VERDI_HOME <VERDI_INST_DIR>
setenv VCATB_SEARCH_PATH <SEARCH_DIRs>
* You need to download the VIP release from SolvNetPlus, perform the installation,
and set DESIGNWARE_HOME environment variable. For details on VIP installation and
environment setting, see the VIP documentation available in SolvNetPlus.
* After setting the DESIGNWARE_HOME environment variable, run the $DESIGNWARE_HOME/
bin/dw_vip_setup utility. This utility adds the VIP models to your project path. It
also sets the VCATB_DESIGN_DIR environment variable to that path. For details on the
dw_vip_setup utility, see the VIP User Guide.
* Synopsys VC VIP includes VIP IP-XACT; you can find the VIP IP-XACT under the VIP
installation, that is, when you set the DESIGNWARE_HOME environment variable. The VIP
IP-XACT is present at: $DESIGNWARE_HOME/vip/svt/<vip>/latest/ipxact

IP-XACT Overview
The IP-XACT standard describes an XML Schema for metadata documenting Intellectual
Property (IP) used in development, implementation, and verification of electronic
systems. This schema provides a standard method to document IP that is compatible with
automated integration techniques.

IP-XACT Overview

The IP-XACT standard is an electronic databook of all the IPs on the chip with their
configuration details. It contains the block-level information with details on how the
components are configured, such as,
* Modes of operation
* Register maps
* Address space
* Interface configuration
* Language and more details
It uses the XML standard to represent the data. For details, see http://ieeexplore.ieee.org/
document/6898803/.

Protocol IP-XACT

Protocol IP-XACT
Protocol IP-XACT defines the notion of a bus definition whose attributes comprise of the
Vendor, Library, Name, and Version (VLNV) signature. This signature determines which
other IP is connected to the bus interface.
Each bus definition from Accellera, other vendors (such as ARM), or Synopsys
consists of two separate XML files. One XML file defines a construct designated by the
spirit:busDefinition XML tag. The other XML file defines a construct designated by
the spirit:abstractionDefinition XML tag.
The AMBA-specific protocol IP-XACT is present in the Verdi installation. You can point the
tool to the following path:
$VERDI_HOME/etc/protocol_ipxact/

DUT IP-XACT
The DUT IP-XACT file defines an IP-XACT component definition. The IP-XACT
specification defines an IPXACT component as follows:
An IP-XACT component is used to describe the meta-data associated with any IP that can
be instantiated in a design.
For determining the overall structure of the testbench, the DUT IP-XACT defines a
collection of bus interfaces to which other blocks can be connected. In the case of VC
AutoTestbench, these DUT bus interfaces are connected to one or more VIPs.

IP-XACT Overview

The DUT IP-XACT component describes all the bus interfaces that can be connected to
VIP instances. For the tool to enable connections between the DUT and one or more VIPs,
the bus interfaces that are referenced by the DUT IP-XACT must be standard protocol bus
interfaces that are known to be compatible with the VIPs that are available to the user.
Further, VLNV for each of the DUT-specified bus interfaces must exactly match VLNV of
at least one VIP to make a legal connection between the DUT and a VIP. The IP-XACT
standard specifies this strict matching requirement.
You must generate the DUT IP-XACT while generating the RTL/Verilog files for the DUT.
If you are using ARM tools, or Synopsys Core tools or Arteris tools and so on to generate
the RTL, you must also generate the IP-XACT file for that DUT from the tool.

VIP IP-XACT
The VIP IP-XACT files describe VIPs with bus interfaces. The following are the two types
of Port-Level VIP IP-XACT definitions:
* Port-level IP-XACT descriptions correspond to single port VIPs. Examples include AHB
master, AXI slave, and CSI2.
* System-level IP-XACT descriptions correspond to system VIPs. Examples include AHB
system and AMBA system. These VIPs consist of port-level VIPs and other systemlevel VIPs.
System-level VIPs can include port-level VIPs and other system-level VIPs. The systemlevel IP-XACT descriptions reference the port-level IP-XACT descriptions. They also
reference other system-level IP-XACT descriptions.
Port-level and system-level VIPs are building blocks for system-level VIPs. Likewise, portlevel and system-level IP-XACT descriptions are building blocks for other system-level IPXACT descriptions.
To summarize, port-level VIP IP-XACT definitions describe stand-alone VIPs or VIP
building blocks. These blocks specify bus interfaces that can connect to DUT bus
interfaces. They can also connect to other testbench components in theory. The section on
Port-Level VIP IP-XACT definitions describes how this connection is determined.
You must set the DESIGNWARE_HOME variable to the VIP installation to get the VIP IP-XACT
files.
In the VC AutoTestbench flow, the VLNV must exactly match between the DUT IP-XACT
and the Protocol IP-XACT. This match is required to connect a DUT interface to a VIP
interface. If there is a mismatch, you cannot connect a VIP on that DUT bus.

The VC AutoTestbench window contains three panes:
* Project Pane
* Testbench Connections Pane
* Configuration Pane

The VC AutoTestbench window layout is illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 368

VC AutoTestbench Window Layout

Project Pane
The Project pane includes three tabs: ProjectTab/View, IP-XACT Tab/View, and DUT
Connections Tab/View.

ProjectTab/View
The complete project information is listed in the Project Tab/View. The following right-click
options are available in the Project tab:
* Show Navigation Text Field: Displays the search field/bar to aid searching in the
Project tab.
* Edit Project: Edits an existing project.

Figure 369

Project Tab/View

IP-XACT Tab/View
The IP-XACT tab lists all the interfaces from DUT IP-XACT files, VIP IP-XACT files,
and protocol IP-XACT files. It also lists the VLNV (vendor, library, name, and version)
information. The following right-click options are available in the IP-XACT tab:
* Show Navigation Text Field: Displays the search field/bar to aid searching in the IPXACT tab.
Figure 370

IP-XACT Tab/View

DUT Connections Tab/View
The DUT Connections tab lists all interfaces and signals for a DUT, parameters of an
instance and information from DUT IP-XACT files. The following columns are present in
this tab:
* Signal: This column shows the physical signal name.
* Logical Name: This column shows the logical name of the physical signal, if the signal
is a part of a bus.
* Connection: This column shows the interface or signal connection. For a DUT instance,
the number of connected buses or the number of buses that can be connected is
shown. The Connection column could be an interface signal, clock/reset generator
(for a clock/reset signal), or a signal driver. Some physical signals are shared by
multiple interfaces and these are listed in the Shared Signals section. For such signals,
connections can only be changed from the Shared Signal section.
The Parameters section displays all parameters of an instance. Double-click the
Connection column to change the value of the selected parameter.
If a signal is selected, the interface signal which is connected to this signal in the TB
Connections tab is highlighted. Different icons are shown for input, output, and inout signal
nodes.
Figure 371

DUT Connections Tab

Support for DUT Parameters
VC AutoTestbench enables you to perform the following actions:
* Set the parameter value to define how the top instance is instantiated in the DUT
wrapper for the DUT top component in a parameterized module.
* Add or correct the parameters value in the IP-XACT file in case of missing or incorrect
values for the IP-XACT flow.
The Parameters section in the DUT Connections tab displays all parameters of an
instance. The parameter value is displayed in the Connection column of the DUT
Connections tab. You can double-click the Connection column to change the value of the
selected parameter.
The following figure illustrates the Parameters section:

To remove the selected parameter, use the Remove right-click option.
To add a new parameter, perform the following steps:
* Select Parameters in the Signal column and use the Add New Parameter right-click
option. The Add New Parameter form opens, as illustrated in the following figure:

title: 1 2012 in default config
text:
* In the Add New Parameter form, enter the new parameter name and value.
The Name field should not be empty; it should be unique and case sensitive. No special
characters are allowed; only alphabets and underscore are allowed.
The Value field can be empty and can accept any kind of values.
The parameter display and edit functionality supports only the IP-XACT flow
and not the KDB flow.
For details on batch mode support for DUT parameters, see Support for DUT Parameters
(Batch Mode)

Support for Creating Bus Interface for IP-XACT Flow
Creating new bus interfaces for selected DUT instance in the IPXACT flow is also
supported. The Create Bus right-click option is enabled on selecting the DUT Connections
tab and the created bus is listed directly under the instance as shown in the following
figure.
Figure 372

text:
Create Bus Option

Creating a Bus Interface for a Project
To create a bus interface for a project, perform the following steps:
1. In the DUT Connections tab, select an instance (a top module or a lower-level
instance). Click the Create Bus right-click option. The Create Bus form opens as
shown in the following figure:
Figure 373

Create Bus Form

title: 1 2012 in default config
text:
2. In the Create Bus form, perform the following steps:
a. In the Name field, enter the name of the bus.
b. In the Mode field, enter the mode of the bus whose value can be Master, Slave,
MirroredMaster, or MirroredSlave.
c. In the Definition field, specify the VLNV information of the bus definition. Select its
value from the available VLNV information loaded from protocol IP-XACT files.
d. If there are multiple bus abstractions available for the specified bus definition, the
Abstraction field is enabled to specify the required abstraction, if not, it is disabled.
e. The Dut Port Signals field displays all port signals of the selected instance.
f. The Bus Signals field displays a signal list of the selected bus. For the selected
bus, the logical signals of the bus are listed in the table view. For each of the logical
signals, you must assign a physical signal. When you click a bus logical signal, the

title: 1 2012 in default config
text:
DUT Port Signals list is ordered by the possibility of matching; the most possible
matched DUT port signal is highlighted.
g. Select Auto Connect to automatically connect all logical signals to the most
possible matches from DUT port signals.
h. Select Connect to connect the selected bus signal to the selected DUT port signal.
i. Select Disconnect to disconnect a connected bus signal.
j. Select Reset to clear all connections.
k. After all connections are assigned, click OK button to create the bus.
After you create a bus, the created bus is listed directly under the instance, as shown in
Figure 374

Created Bus

Component Fileset Settings
VC AutoTestbench provides you the component fileset setting to specify more information
to build a component.

To set the component fileset, select the Fileset Setting right-click option, as illustrated in

The following figure illustrates the Fileset Setting form that appears on selecting the
Fileset Setting right-click option:

The Fileset Setting form has the following two parts:
* The first part is for the selected instance to choose a view, if there are multiple views
for the component of that instance. If there is only one view, the combo box for view
selection is disabled. If there is only one fileset (without view), then the fileset is used
as the default view.
* The second part is the setting for the component of the selected instance. Here, you
can choose the view to change settings. You can turn on/off each of the switch and
add additional compiler directives. If there is only one view, the combo box for view
selection is disabled. If there is only one fileset (without view), then the fileset is used
as the default view.
For details on batch mode for component fileset settings, see Component Fileset Settings
(Batch Mode).

Overriding the Testbench Top
If you want to use your own DUT wrapper instead of using the one generated by the tool,
you need to specify the module name of the provided wrapper and the full path of the DUT
inside the wrapper module.
The following figure shows the flow:

1. To enable the user-provided testbench top, you can specify the module name, the
DUT path, and the instance name in the Testbench Top field in the Edit Project form
(invoked using File -> Edit Project menu option in VC ATB GUI).
Figure 375

Defining Testbench Top

When Testbench Top is selected, you must specify values in Module, DUT Path, and
Instance fields.
If the Testbench Top field is enabled, then the DUT top name in both DUT Connections
and IP-XACT tabs is changed to the DUT path name specified.

For details on overriding the testbench top using batch mode, see Overriding the
Testbench Top (Batch Mode).
You have the flexibility to define the Testbench Top module, and provide the module name
to the tool.
To define the Testbench Top module, perform the following steps:
1. In the VC AutoTestbench window, click the File -> New Project menu command.
2. In theCreate Project form, select the Advanced tab.
3. Enable the Testbench Top option.
4. Define the module name in the Module field, DUT path in DUT Path field, and the
instance name in the Instance field. All the fields are enabled by default to enter the
values. The Module and DUT path are mandatory fields and Instance is an optional
field. If the instance name is not provided then the module_inst name is used as the
default name. The Instance name must be provided along with the Module name and
the validation check is done accordingly.
The following right-click options are available in the DUT Connections tab:
* Show Navigation Text Field: Displays the search field/bar to aid searching in the DUT
Connections tab.
* Add New VIP: Adds a new top level VIP instance for the selected DUT buses.
* Connect to VIP: Connects the selected DUT buses to the specified VIP instance.

* Connect: Sets connections for clock/reset/signal.
* Disconnect: Disconnects the selected signals or buses.
* Create Internal Clock: Creates an internal clock from the selected signal.
* Create Internal Reset: Creates an internal reset from the selected signal.
* Set As Clock: Selects the required signal that is recognized as clock.
* Set As Reset: Selects the required signal that is recognized as reset.
* Set Replaceable: Sets the selected DUT instance or internal instance as replaceable.
* Fileset Setting: Allows you to set the root directory of the file set (the set of
implementation HDL files for a DUT instance is called a file set of that instance) and
select the view to be used by the testbench.
* The file set of one instance could have multiple views, each for a different
implementation (a different set of files). For example, one view for Verilog
implementation and another for VHDL implementation. For more information on file set
setting, see Component Fileset Settings.
* Set Top Instance : Sets the selected instance as the top instance.
* Create Bus: Invokes the Create Bus form.
* Edit Bus: Invokes the Create Bus form to edit an existing bus.
* Delete Bus: Deletes the selected bus.
* Save IP-XACT: Invokes the File form to save IP-XACT files for the DUT. IP-XACT files
are saved for the entire DUT system, including all internal components.
* Apply IP-XACT: Applies an existing IP-XACT file (may include IP-XACT files for
internal instances) to the selected DUT instance. After the IP-XACT file is applied to the
instance, buses defined in the IP-XACT file for the instance (and its child instances) are
populated
* Detach IP-XACT: Detaches the applied IP-XACT file from the selected instance.
* Add New Parameter: Invokes the Add New Parameter form to add a new parameter.
This option is enabled only on selecting an item in the Parameters section.
* Remove: Removes the selected parameter.

Testbench Connections Pane
This pane shows the testbench hierarchy, clock/reset generators, and signal drivers. It
shows the connected interfaces for a component that has virtual interfaces. Each interface

Configuration Tab/View
This tab/view shows the configuration for VIP instances.
When you select a VIP instance in the TB Connections pane, the configuration of that
instance is displayed in the Configuration pane as illustrated in the following figure:

Configuration Pane

You can double-click items in the Value column to change the value for any non-constant

Support for VIP Properties at Global Level
VC AutoTestbench application is enhanced to set the required attribute values common to
all instances in the environment or common to all instances globally to all environments.
In the Configurations tab, right-click and select the Set as Global Flag option or Set All
Instances on ENV Flag option.
Figure 380

Setting Attributes

Following is the list of right-click menu options available for the Configurations tab:
* Set as Global Flag:This command selects the attribute values and update all other
VIP instances in all environments globally and attributes are synchronized. Any change
in the attribute value is applied to other instances globally across the environment
variables. The selected attribute background is highlighted in yellow color as shown in

Figure 381

* Set All Instances on ENV Flag: This command selects the attribute values

Support for Memory Map
VC AutoTestbench is enhanced to visualize the memory map information and map
the information into the design through configuration. The memory map information

is displayed in the Memory Maps tab present in the Configuration pane of the VC
AutoTestbench window. You can also create a memory map or add new memory map
details using the Memory Maps tab/view.
Memory Map Details in the IP-XACT File
The following sections are present in the IP-XACT file that contain the memory map
information:
* busInterfaces
It contains the list of bus interfaces. This list is used by VC AutoTestbench to derive
Initiator and Target values. All the slave bus interfaces are represented as Initiators and
all the master bus interfaces are represented as Targets.
* addressSpaceRef (Master busInterface), baseAddress
The addressSpaceRef section resides on a master bus interface. It provides a
reference of an addressSpace element that can be viewed by the master. Some of the
Master busInterface provides baseAddress, which is the base address reference.
* memoryMapRef (Slave busInterface)
The memoryMapRef section resides on a slave bus interface (Initiator). It provides a
reference of the memory map view of that element.
* addressSpaces
It shows the addressSpace viewed by a master bus interface (Target).
* memoryMaps
It mainly represents the following two areas:
Subspace elements that consist of masterRef and/or segmentRef attributes and it
consists of the base address for that memory.
Address blocks and register maps for that component.

<spirit:abstractionType spirit:version="r0p0_0"
spirit:vendor="arm.com" spirit:name="AXI_ext_rtl"
spirit:library="PL301"/>
<spirit:slave>

Memory Map Terminologies
The initiators (slave interface) and targets (master interface) are derived from the IPXACT file. The memory map information across each initiator target can be represented as
* Local Address
At Initiator: The localAddress is the start address (base address) of the
addressSpace that an Initiator can access. From IP-XACT perspective,
localAddress is same as globalAddress, since IP-XACT does not differentiate
between both of these.
At Target: The localAddress is the base address of the target device
* Global Address
At Initiator: The Global Address is the start address (base address) in the system
memory, which gets actually mapped to the Initiator's local address. From IP-XACT
perspective, they are same at Initiator.
If the memory represented is a sparse memory, that is, segments, the
initiator always shows the least address. For example, if the memory is
sparse, like, 0x0 0x100 0x200 0x300, then the global address is 0x0. The
Range is the complete range specified by the addressSpace in the IP-XACT
file.
* At Target: The Global Address is the start address (base address) in the system
memory, which gets mapped to the target device's local address.
* Range
At Initiator: This is the total address range an initiator can access in its address
space starting from the baseAddress.

initiator always shows the least address. For example, if the memory is

Creating Project for Large Designs
For creating projects for large designs, the following are the best practices:
* Ignore any specific modules having the given names.
* Consider only the required modules having the given name.
* Ignore the module which is not needed for testbench generation and this gradually
increases the tool performance.

GUI Proposal
Include Only the Required Modules
The environment variable VCATB_INCLUDE_MODULES_FILE can be used to choose only
the required top DUT modules in the final project creation. The following is the command
used:
setenv VCATB_INCLUDE_MODULES_FILE <Filepath>

The file should be of RC file format. Required sub modules full path should be specified for
option names inside the MODULE_NAMES section as shown in the following figure.

The DUT and the Testbench are connected through interface and connection details
(interface and signals), which are displayed in the Connection column of DUT Connections
and TB Connections tabs, as illustrated in the following figure:

Some interfaces may have multiple instances that share some system-level signals. For
example, the following figure shows multiple AHB instances that share signals such as
hrdata_bus, hready_bus, hresp_bus, and so on; in this case, the system-level signals
appear on AHB system for master instance, but not on single instance.

Internal Clock/Reset
If you want to use the internal clock/reset block defined in the DUT, you must create an
internal clock/reset block from the internal DUT signals.
Note that, an internal DUT signal must be an output signal with width 1, to be qualified as
a source of an internal clock/reset.

To create an internal clock/reset block, select the DUT signal and select Create Internal
Clock or Create Internal Reset right-click options.
Figure 393

Create Internal Clock

After the internal clock/reset is created, it is listed in the Clock Generator section of the TB
Connections tab. You can connect any clock/reset signal to this internal clock/reset. The
internal clock/reset cannot be edited, but it can be removed and a new internal clock/reset
can be connected to the same DUT signal.

Clock/Reset Connections
The following RMB actions are added to DUT Connections tab:
* Set as Clock
* Set as Reset
You can select the required signal to recognize it as clock/reset. A tick mark indicates
that this signal is a clock or reset. Select the action again from the same signal to DeRecognize as clock/reset. These actions are disabled when DUT clock/reset is already
available or qualified using protocol IP-XACT files.

Figure 394

Set as Clock/Reset

At connection time, UserDefined is appended at the end. This differentiates user-defined
clock/reset from qualified clock/reset. See the following figure:
Figure 395

DUT Clock in Clock Generator

Following are the limitations of the Clock/Reset connections:
* You cannot De-Recognize clock/reset signal if its already connected. In such cases,
you should remove the connection first and De-Recognize clock/reset signal.
* You can know the chosen clock/reset signals only from Clock Generator connect
action.
* Batch mode is not supported.

Signal Level Connection
By default, after you connect a DUT bus to a VIP instance, signals from the bus are
connected automatically. You can drag and drop a DUT signal to a virtual interface signal
(and vice versa) to build the customized DUT-VIP signal connection.
To connect to a signal driver, you can either select the signal driver from the Connect
right-click option or drag and drop the signal to the signal driver (and vice versa).
To connect to a user-specified constant value, double-click the Connection column of the
signal and then enter the constant value.

To highlight all the connections, select the Highlight All Connections right-click option in
the DUT Connections tab.
You can use the Show Connection right-click option in the TB Connections pane to
display all connections in the sub-menu; you can then select a specific connection to view
it.

Figure 396

Show Connection

If a DUT instance includes other instances, and the internal DUT IPXACT files are
available, VC AutoTestbench displays internal instances at the end in the DUT
Connections tab (after the Adhoc Signals section).

Support to Read the VCATB VIP Related Files
The environment variable VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE is supported to read the VCATB
VIP related files. The following command is used:
setenv VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE <Directory Path>

Only one path is allowed in the new environment variable. Therefore, it assumes the
environment variable value as one directory path.
/dir1/dir2/dir3//verdi_vcatb_vip_files

Multiple paths for VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE are not supported. In such cases, the tool
logs an error message in the vcatb.log file. The following command is used:
setenv VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE <path1>:<path2>:<path3>

The following types of error messages are logged into vcatb.log file based on the issue
while reading the path:
Examples of error messages:
Error. `VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE' referred path <{<Value>} is not valid. Multiple
paths are not allowed.
Error. `VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE' referred path <{<Value>} is not found
Error. `VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE' referred path <{<Value>} is not a valid directory
path. It's a file path
Error. `VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE' referred path <{<Value>} does not have read
permissions. Hence cannot read VCATB related files

Folder Structure
Structure of the VCATB VIP files in VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE locations as shown below:
$VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE/$vip_name/$version
$VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE/$vip_name/latest ./ $version

<path1>/amba_svt/R-2020.12/ipxact
<path1>/amba_svt/R-2020.12/vcatb

Multiple VCATB VIP related files can also be added into the VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE
location as shown in the following examples:
<path1>/lpddr_svt
<path1>/spi_svt
<path1>/amba_svt

You can override custom/third-party `VIP' details also using VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE
variable.
Referring Using the Latest Version
Tool updates the VIP details including version number in the Tcl variables. Therefore,
you should use the right version for VIP referred in VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE location.
Following are the examples:
vcatb_vip_suites.0.is_fixed = 0
vcatb_vip_suites.0.name = amba_svt
vcatb_vip_suites.0.version = R-2020.12

Tool always considers the `latest' version referred in VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE location
while updating the vcatb_vip_suites Tcl variables. Therefore, it is recommended to use
the right VIP version.
If VIP `latest' version in VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE location is different from
DESIGNWARE_HOME, then you should unset the VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE location.
Support for Multiple VIP Versions
VIP details added in VCATB_VIP_PATH_OVERRIDE location should have the latest link
referring to the required version. Following are the examples:
<path1>/amba_svt/R-2020.12
<path1>/amba_svt/latest ./ R-2020.12

Even when multiple versions are available, you should set the required version as latest.
Following are the examples:
<path1>/amba_svt/R-2020.12
<path1>/amba_svt/R-2020.09

<path1>/amba_svt/P-2019.03
<path1>/amba_svt/latest ./ R-2020.12

Importing KDB Library
To import the design, use either the command line options or click the File -> Import
Design menu option in the Verdi GUI.
On clicking the File -> Import Design menu option, the Import Design form opens as
illustrated in the following figure.

title: 1 2012 in default config
text:
For details on importing the KDB library into Verdi, see the Verdi documentation.

Creating a DUT KDB Library Project
You can create a DUT KDB library project by importing a KDB into Verdi. If the KDB
is imported into Verdi, the from KDB checkbox in the Create Project form is selected/
checked and a DUT KDB library based project is created. For a DUT KDB library based
project, the DUT IP-XACT field in the Create Project form is disabled.
Figure 398

The Create Project Form

After a KDB library based project is created, the Project tab, the IP-XACT tab, and the
DUT Connections tab in the VC AutoTestbench pane are populated automatically. In the
IP-XACT tab, the DUT section includes only the top DUT instance node and there are no
buses under the instance node. After you create a bus from the signals, it is listed under
the relative DUT instance. If the project is created using KDB, opening the project loads
the design automatically.

The IP-XACT tab is illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 399

The IP-XACT Tab

In the DUT Connections tab, the complete instance hierarchy is displayed. By default, only
the top instance is expanded. For each instance, all the port signals are listed in the Adhoc
Signals section. You can select an instance and create a bus interface for the selected
instance from the Adhoc Signals section. The DUT Connections tab is illustrated in the
Figure 400

DUT Connections Tab

Creating a Bus Interface for a Project
To create a bus interface for a project, perform the following steps:
1. In the DUT Connections tab, select an instance (a top module or a lower-level
instance), and click the Create Bus right-click option. The Create Bus form opens as
illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 401

Create Bus Form

title: 1 2012 in default config
text:
2. In the Create Bus form,
a. In the Name field, enter the name of the bus.
b. In the Mode field, enter the mode of the bus whose value could be Master, Slave,
MirroredMaster, or MirroredSlave.
c. In the Definition field, specify the VLNV information of the bus definition. Select its
value from the available VLNV information loaded from protocol IP-XACT files.
d. If there are multiple bus abstractions available for the specified bus definition, the
Abstraction field is enabled to specify the required abstraction, otherwise it is
disabled.
e. The Dut Port Signals field displays all port signals of the selected instance.

title: 1 2012 in default config
text:
f. The Bus Signals field displays a signal list of the selected bus. For the selected
bus, the logical signals of the bus are listed in the table view. For each of the logical
signals, you must assign a physical signal.
When you click a bus logical signal, the DUT Port Signals list is ordered by the
possibility of matching; the most possible matched DUT port signal is highlighted.
The following rules are used to calculate the possibility of matching and locate the
most possible physical signals for the selected bus logical signal:
If the direction of the physical signal matches the direction of the logical signal
If the width of the physical signal is the same as the width of the logical signal
If the physical signal name includes the bus name or includes a substring that is
similar to the bus name
If the physical name includes the logical name or includes a substring that is
similar to the logical name
g. In some cases where the DUT port signals names are not related to the bus and the
logical signal name, the rules may not work as expected.
h. Use the Auto Connect button to automatically connect all logical signals to the
most possible matches from DUT port signals.
i. Use the Connect button to connect the selected bus signal to the selected DUT
port signal.
j. Use the Disconnect button to disconnect a connected bus signal.
k. Use the Reset button to clear all connections.
l. After all connections are assigned, click the OK button to create the bus.
After you create a bus, the created bus is listed directly under the instance, as
illustrated in the following figure:

If any of the port signals are used by the created bus, then these signals are removed from
the AdHoc Signals section. If any port signals are used by multiple created buses, then
these signals are listed in the Share Signal section.
After a bus is created for the selected instance,
* The same bus is applied to all other instances from the same module, if all the signals
of the bus are available and have the same definition (type, width, direction, and so
on) for a parameterized module; the parameter value may affect the signature of the
module, for example the existence, the width or the direction of some signals.
* The same bus is created for the outer instance, if the bus is exported to the outer
instance. For example, if a bus is created for the top.cpu0 instance and all signals of
the bus are connected to the port signals of top, then the same bus is created for the
top instance.
After all buses are created for the imported DUT, use the Save IP-XACT right-click option
to save an IP-XACT file for the entire DUT system, including the created bus interfaces.
Next time, when you work on the same DUT, you can use the saved IP-XACT instead of
the KDB.

Multiple Top Instances
Testbench generation supports a single top instance. However, if the KDB library includes
multiple top instances, you can set one of the top instances as the target top DUT
instance.
The testbench generation supports the target top instance. The icon for the target top
instance is marked with a red dot, as illustrated in the following figure:
Figure 402

Target Top Instance

For KDB that includes multiple top instances, the first instance is set as the target top
instance by default. To set any other instance as the top instance, select the instance, and
click the Set Top Instance right-click option.

Replace and Connect Functionality
The generated testbench supports replace and connect functionalities. When a component
is selected as a replaceable component, you can decide if you want to use the bus
interface as an active VIP or a passive VIP. While using the generated testbench, you can
choose to use one of the following modes:
* Connect Mode (Passive Connect)
This mode enables you to connect the buses of a component or an internal instance to
specified VIP instances. When an actual RTL (original RTL instance) is connected to
the bus interface, the VIP is connected as passive mode. This passive VIP can then be
used to monitor traffic across that connection.
* Replace Mode (Active Replace)
This mode enables you to set a component or an internal instance as replaceable.
When there is no RTL connected to the interface, an active VIP gets connected to that
interface as a replacement for the original RTL instance. You can then use the VIP
capabilities to drive traffic at that interface.
The prerequisite for both active replace or passive connect is that in addition
to supporting an SV interface, the VIP must support a corresponding SV bind
interface.
To enable Passive Connect and Active Replace modes, perform the following steps:
1. Set your internal connection, that is, connect a component internal to the DUT with a
VIP in the AMBA system environment.
a. In the DUT Connections tab, select the component that you want to replace, and
select the Set Replaceable right-click option.
b. Click the '+' next to the component to view the internal components.
c. Select the item and use the Connect to VIP right-click option to connect to the
desired VIP.

2. Use the same defines for CONNECT as present in the output_dir/dut_wrapper/
dut_wrapper.sv file and the gmake command to enable Passive Connect mode. For
example:
gmake clean sanity_test CMDLINE_COMP_ARGS='+define+<CONNECT Define
present in the dut_wrapper.sv>'

3. Use the same defines for REPLACE as present in the output_dir/dut_wrapper/
dut_wrapper.sv file and the gmake command to enable Active Replace mode. For
example:
gmake clean sanity_test CMDLINE_COMP_ARGS='+define+<REPLACE Define
present in the dut_wrapper.sv>'

The name for CONNECT and REPLACE define present in the
dut_wrapper.sv file is based on the path to the instance being connected
or replaced combined with the DUT busRef name. For example, for
the following design XML, the resulting define for CONNECT would be
VCATB_CONNECT_SUBSYSTEM_A15_CCI500_I_CORTEXA15_1_AXI4MASTER

and the resulting define for REPLACE would be

Support for PHY Integration

Demo Examples
The demo examples for VC AutoTestbench are available at: $VERDI_HOME/demo/
vcatb. For details on how to execute the examples, refer to the README file at the same
location.

Support for PHY Integration
Point-to-point controller IP requires the use of a PHY to drive the physical signaling. The
controller IP provides a parallel bus interface, which is connected to the PHY simulation
model. The PHY model is typically provided separately from the IP model, and you must
connect the IP controller to the PHY model.
The VC AutoTestbench flow identifies situations where a PHY is required and generates
a testbench with a PHY Shell module that is connected to the DUT and to the VIP. To
complete the testbench integration, you must replace the PHY shell module with a module
that wraps your PHY simulation model.

Prerequisite
PHY integration requires a protocol IP-XACT description for both bus interfaces. You
need one for the parallel PHY bus interface and one for the serial PHY bus interface. If a
standard protocol IP-XACT is not available, develop it and ship it with the appropriate VIP.
If DUT IP-XACT does not support the required protocol IP-XACT, then an adjunct file
must be developed that exposes these bus interfaces and allows them to be connected to
testbench elements.

Serial Interface From DUT Side
If DUT IP-XACT exposes a serial PHY bus interface, this implies that a PHY model
is integrated into the DUT and is connected to the IP Controller. In this situation, the
testbench element is connected directly to the exposed PHY serial bus interface in the
DUT.

Parallel Interface From DUT Side
If DUT IP-XACT exposes a parallel PHY bus interface, this implies that a parallel PHY bus
interface connection is required. Some VIP titles support a direct connection to the parallel
PHY bus interface. Therefore, VC AutoTestbench provides you an option to select either
the VIP's parallel PHY bus interface or the VC ATB PHY shell module.
If you select the VIP's parallel PHY bus interface, then the VC ATB connects to it directly.

Support for PHY Integration

If you select to use the PHY shell module, then the VC ATB creates and connects a
compatible PHY shell module in the generated testbench. In this case, you also need to
choose one serial bus from the available serial bus list.

If you choose to use the PHY shell module, then the VC ATB creates and connects a
compatible PHY shell module in the generated testbench.
The following points characterize this feature:
* VC ATB identifies the compatible VIP by recognizing the parallel PHY bus interface in
DUT IP-XACT.
* VIP IP-XACT defines a serial PHY bus interface (or bus interfaces in the case of
multiple lanes) that is associated with the parallel PHY bus interface.
* VC ATB supports n-to-1 or 1-to-n ratios of parallel-to-serial interfaces for the PHY shell
module.
* If there are multiple serial PHY bus interfaces that map to a parallel PHY bus interface,
VCATB allows you to select which serial PHY bus interface must be used.
The PHY shell module is composed of a parallel bus interface and one or more serial bus
interfaces. The PHY shell module is non-functional. It defines a Verilog module with the
appropriate port interface to represent a PHY model.
For VIPs that support a parallel PHY bus interface connection, you can connect the VIP
to the parallel PHY bus interface of the PHY Shell module. This enables the generated
testbench to be functional.
For VIPs that do not support a parallel PHY bus interface, you must replace the PHY Shell
module with your PHY simulation model.
The parallel PHY bus interface of the PHY shell module is defined by the DUT IP-XACT.
The serial PHY bus interface (or bus interfaces in the case of multiple lanes) is identified
by the VIP IP-XACT. VCATB uses these bus interfaces to determine the signals required
by the PHY shell module. It connects the PHY shell module to DUT and VIP appropriately.
These signals are communicated to the template engine using Tcl variables. This allows
the PHY Shell module can be generated. The signal connections are communicated using
Tcl variables. This enables the PHY Shell module can be instantiated and connected in the
DUT Wrapper.
After the testbench has been generated, you must replace the PHY Shell module with
your simulation model. You can use the VC ATB User Extension feature and make use
of Verilog 2001 configuration capabilities to accomplish this. This can be done without
modifying the generated testbench..

Support for PHY Integration

In GUI mode, you can select whether you want to directly connect to the VIP provided
parallel PHY interface or use the PHY Shell module at the VIP selection step.

Support for PHY Integration

In GUI mode, you can select whether you want to directly connect to the VIP provided
parallel PHY interface or use the PHY Shell module at the VIP selection step. If the
PHY shell module is selected, then VC AutoTestbench shows this in the testbench
hierarchy. The PHY shell module is presented like any other testbench element. It allows
for signal connection overrides in both the GUI and the config.ini file. After the testbench is
generated, you must replace the PHY Shell module with your simulation model.
Connecting to VIP
For a DUT PHY bus, you need to select not only the VIP to connect, but also how to
connect to the VIP. You can use PHY shell connection (serial) or direct connection
(parallel). For the PHY shell connection, you need to select which serial interface must be
used.
The Add New VIP right-click option lists all combinations of the possible selections. For
example, for the PCIE bus, the matched VIP is svt_pcie_device_agent. It supports both
parallel and serial connections. For serial connection, two different versions of serial
interfaces are available. Therefore, there are total of 3 different kinds of connections
supported. For each of them, the connection type and VLNV are displayed in the menu
title.

If you choose to connect a PHY bus through serial connection, the tool generates a PHY
shell module that is connected to the DUT and to the VIP. The PHY module is listed in the
TB Connections tab as a new section - PHY Module. For each module instance, all the
port signals are listed.

User Extensions

For details on the batch mode use model, see Support for PHY Integration.

User Extensions
User extensions allow you to develop and maintain your own extended codes. You can
modify the testbench and can keep the modified files under the user created user_env
and user_tests directories. By default, the extensions use the term 'user' in their file
names, variable names, object names, and so on.
The following sub-sections explain the available extensions.

Name and Location Alternatives
* Naming
You can optionally specify a prefix value to be used for file names, variable
names, object names, code elements and so on. This can be done either in the
GUI or in the [USER EXTENSIONS] section of config.ini. The specified prefix
replaces the default prefix - user in all the code references. However, this does not
apply to the "Makefile Only" controls, such as, USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR and
USER_EXTENSIONS_TESTS_DIR. For example, if you specify proj1 as the prefix,
then every user in the name is proj1 instead, such as, proj1_vcatb_base_test.sv,
proj1_vcatb_env.sv, and so on.
If no prefix is specified, the default prefix - "user" is used.

User Extensions

* Directory Locations
You can specify the path/value of environment directory and/or test directory. This
can be done either in the GUI or in the [USER EXTENSIONS] section of config.ini.
Set the USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR value in Makefile.cfg to env_dir and the
USER_EXTENSIONS_TESTS_DIR value in Makefile.cfg to tests_dir. User-provided
environment files and test files are pulled from the specified env_dir and tests_dir
directories respectively.
In order to incorporate user extensions, you must specify either the env_dir value or
the tests_dir value. If neither of these values is specified, the user extension support
is disabled.

Extending the Top Level Testbench
This feature allows you to insert content into the module defined by the vcatb_top.sv file.
There are two following two insertion points:
* Content provided in the user_top_includes.sv file which is inserted before the
vcatb_top module is declared. This allows for additional files to be included.
* Content provided by user_top.sv file is inserted at the end of the vcatb_top module.

User Extensions

Both files must be placed in the $USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR directory. If these files are
present then they are automatically included by the generated testbench.
Based on its placement, this code can reference vcatb_top.sv content, if necessary. This
should be done sparingly, however, to avoid dependencies on specific naming, content,
and so on.

Extending the Testbench and Test Management
The testbench management can be adjusted by providing environment and test
implementations for different methodology-defined phases. To support this create
user versions of vcatb_base_test.sv (that is, $USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR/
user_vcatb_base_test.sv) and vcatb_env.sv (that is, $USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR/
user_vcatb_env.sv) files which include the desired adjustments.
If the files are available, these are included automatically and the Auto Testbench versions
of these files are extended from their user counterparts. For example,
* class vcatb_base_test extends user_vcatb_base_test;
* class vcatb_env extends user_vcatb_env;

Support for Additional Tests
To provide additional tests using the user extension flow, the additional tests must
be placed in the $USER_EXTENSIONS_TESTS_DIR directory. You must also create a
user_test_package.sv file located in the $USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR directory. This
file should be modeled after the vcatb_test.pkg file and contain include directives for
all the additional tests. The actual file names (such as, ts.my_test.sv) can be used here,
without any directory prefix, as the $USER_EXTENSIONS_TESTS_DIR directory is added as
an incdir by the Makefile.
The generated Makefile provides additional support for this capability by including
$USER_EXTENSIONS_TESTS_DIR in the list of directories it searches to identify valid test
names.
The generated testbench includes these additional tests by including
$USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR/user_test_package.sv in vcatb_test.pkg
automatically, if available. This automatically includes all of the test files included in the
user_test_package.sv file.
User tests must also adhere to the basic testcase design criteria so that they work properly
in this flow:
* Test classes must extend from vcatb_base_test
* Test files must follow 'ts.*.sv' test file naming convention

Support for Additional Files
In addition to the user test management and user test files , you might have other files
which they need to include into the system. These files are included automatically if they
are specified in a file list stored as $USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR/user_file_list.f.
This file list can include VLOG or SV files, packages or programs, other file lists (file lists
prefaced with the -f option), and so on. The only requirement is that the paths which are
specified in the file list are hard paths. For example, if additional files are stored locally
in $USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR, you need the $USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR/ prefix. If
stored elsewhere on the network, you must specify the files with a relative path or a hard
path.

Extending Build Management
As indicated in the previous sections, there are some build extensions which are built
into the Makefile. In addition, you can also add your own Makefile extension. Create
$USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR/Makefile containing any additional settings you want
to add. The $USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR/Makefile file is included by the top level
Makefile after all of its variables are specified and before any rules are defined.
This can be used to modify any of the top level Makefile variables that are referenced in
the subsequent rules.

Initial User Extension Development
It is recommended to use the GUI or the config.ini process to enable your extensions.
Create user environment and/or test directories, set the appropriate prefix, env_dir, and
tests_dir values in GUI or config.ini, and generate the testbench with this information.
The benefit of following this process is that every regeneration includes all the user
extensions added previously.
During the initial user extension development, however, it might be necessary to forego
some of these steps. For example, you might want to take an existing testbench area,
incorporate some extensions, get them working, and then go back and make them official.
Set env_dir and test values in the original testbench description. You can accomplish
this by modifying the Makefile.cfg file in the generated testbench. You can specify
USER_EXTENSIONS_ENV_DIR and/or USER_EXTENSIONS_TESTS_DIR values. Specifying
either of these values results in enabling the user extensions features and incorporating
the user extensions in the testbench.

User Extensions Flow

Delaying this decision to the `compilation' phase is only supported for the env_dir and
tests_dir settings. It is not supported for the prefix setting. Implementing this support
manually, that is, by modifying Makefile.cfg, also implies that these changes are not
picked up on subsequent testbench generation. That is, env_dir and tests_dir settings
not included in the testbench description are not included in the generated testbench.

User Extensions Flow
* Enter the Testbench features, including the identification of user_env and user_tests
directories.
* Generate original Testbench
Links are automatically established to user_env and user_tests.
* Regenerate the testbench
Links are automatically established to user_env and user_tests.
