FaultRCA: Fault Analysis
FaultRCA consists of the following sections:
* General Fault Analysis
* NC Analysis
* Limitation of FaultRCA

Debugging general faults, such as NO, NN, ND, and so on, means that you need to
trace the fanout from the fault location. Follow the path finding the blocking points in the
downstream circuits until you reach an observation or detection point. This is a timeconsuming process that requires manual efforts.
To overcome the limitation of excessive manual effort and time consumption, FaultRCA
provides utility that helps in detecting the blocking points between the fault-injected point
and the observation or detection point.
A path is created from the fault location to the observation point. Along this path, you can
identify and collect blocking points. This helps you focus on the path and attempt to make
the fault move from the injected point) to the observation point.
Blocking Points
Blocking points are the points through which a fault cannot propagate. For example, as
shown in Figure 209, assume A is the fault location where the fault SA1 (stuck-at-1) is
injected. The fault propagates to C. However, the fault cannot propagate to D.
As the value of B is constantly 0, the primitive AND gate never allows the fault at C to
propagate to D. Because the fault is not propagated to D, the AND cell is called the
blocking cell.

Figure 209

Blocking Cell

This section consists of the following topics:
* Fault Analysis Method
* Running Fault Analysis
* Configuration Fields in the Configuration File
* Generating and Loading Tracing Report in Verdi
* Viewing Tracing Report in Verdi
* Ranking Report

Fault Analysis Method
The fault analysis method provides the following two modes:
* Static Trace Mode
* Block Cell Detection Mode

Static Trace Mode
FaultRCA traces the path from the input fault to the destination point. You can either
extract the observation point from the fault database (FDB) or provide a list of signals to
the tool. You can run this mode in the following two ways:
* Target Signal Mode
* Auto Mode
Target Signal Mode
To analyze one or more signals, use target signal mode. In this mode, you must provide
one or multiple input signals. The information, such as observations list and signal type,
are extracted from the FDB. FaultRCA generates an XML report (.xml) and a text report
(.txt) containing the tracing path.

The format of the fault list file is <Signal Full hierarchy name>. For example,
top.a.b
top.c.d.e

Auto Mode
To analyze a list of critical location points available in the FDB, use auto mode. Auto
mode analyzes more than one signal, and it allows you to select the number of signals to
analyze. The FaultRCA utility automatically analyzes the most critical locations, that is, the
blocking points that cover highest number of NO fault from the FDB. It generates an XML
report and a text report containing tracing paths of all the signals. The information, such as
observation points, signal types, and a list of critical blocking points is extracted from the
FDB.

Block Cell Detection Mode
FaultRCA traces a path between the input fault to the destination point and finds any
blocking cell along the path. You can get the observation point from the FDB or provide
a list of signals to the tool. For this mode, you need the dumped waveform from either a
good machine or faulty machine (gm/fm). One input pin has the GM/FM annotation value.
All output pins have only the GM annotation values.
A block instance on a flip-flop checks the current status of the GM/FM annotation and the
incoming clock cycle. Specifically, it checks the input GM/FM status in the current clock
cycle and the output GM/FM status in the next clock cycle.
When the next clock cycle arrives at the signal connected to the register clock port, the
block checks the clock port. If the clock port is rising or falling, it finds the next rising or
falling time. Otherwise, it finds the next time the value changes.
This mode supports only Stuck@0 and Stuck@1. You can run it in the target signal mode.
Target Signal Mode
If you want to analyze one or multiple signals, use target signal mode. In this mode, you
must provide one or multiple input signals and the target signal list name.
The following is the format of the fault list:
<stuck@0>/<stuck@1>, <Signal full hierarchy name>

0, top.a.b
1, top.c.d.e

Running Fault Analysis
You can run fault analysis using autorca in the static trace mode and the block cell
detection mode.
To generate the configuration file template (run.yaml), use the following command:
autorca -gen_cfg_template <run.yaml> -gen_mode faultrca

When you run the command, the run.yaml file is generated.
The following are the requirements to run fault analysis:
* The simv.daidir directory
* The mode field must be set to 1 by default.
* The gm/fm waveform is required for the block cell detection mode.
For FDB, you must specify the following fields:
* FDB project name: Specify the name of the FDB project to be used.
* FDB path: Specify the full path of the FDB directory.
* Campaign name: Specify the campaign name that is used for dumping FDB.
* For the destination point, you can provide the text file or extract the observation or
detection point from the FDB.
For the target signal mode, you must specify the text file containing the name of the
signals. For more information on the format of the fault list file for the static trace mode
and the block cell detection mode, refer to the Static Trace Mode and Block Cell Detection
Mode sections, respectively.
For the auto mode, specify the number of top critical locations that you require.

Generating and Loading Tracing Report in Verdi
You can generate the tracing report in the .xml and .txt formats using the following

autorca command:

autorca -cfg run.yaml

FaultRCA generates the following types of reports:
* Faultrca_report.xml
* Faultrca_report.txt
* Faultrca_block.xml
* Faultrca_block.txt
You can load the generated report in Verdi using the following command:
autorca -load_report <report_name>.xml

You can view the XML report in Verdi. However, you cannot view the text report
in Verdi.

Ranking Report
The block cell detection mode generates reports in the text and XML formats, for example,
faultrca_block.txt and faultrca_block.xml. In the generated reports, the input
faults are grouped based on the same blocking points. The ranking report is a feature that
prioritizes blocking points with the highest number of input faults and positions them at the
top, as shown in the following figure:
Figure 223

Ranking Report

In Figure 223, the blocking point

or1200_testbench.or1200_top_i.or1200_or1200_sprs(@1):SigOp4:242:242:Combo

groups three input faults, which is more than the input faults grouped under the other
blocking point. Therefore, the blocking point with three input faults is placed at the top.

The Not Controllable (NC) analysis provides a method to reduce manual efforts while
cleaning up the NC faults. NC faults occur in unselected signals during fault simulation.
An NC fault happens when the fanin value stays constant, which makes the fault
uncontrollable.
The existing FDB consists of multiple critical locations, and each critical location consists
of multiple faults. The faults are categorized with common location points to determine
which location point has the maximum number of NC faults. To find the root cause, you
must trace through the NC locations to find the faults where the fanin value remains
constant. This is a time-consuming process.
The NC analysis automates tracing and scans for every NC location, and traces its fanin
cone. The tracing continues until no fanin or all fanin are found with the changed values.
This ensures that the root cause is found. The root cause with the highest number of
critical locations and faults is the top root cause. The report displays the root-cause bucket
containing all the root causes, critical locations, and faults grouped inside the blocking
points.
NC Faults
NC faults are faults that stay constant during simulation. These faults occur when a signal,
which is the input to the fault, does not change its value. That is, the value stays at zero
or one throughout the simulation. The 0-X-0 or 1-X-1 state does not count as switching
states. You must run the fault manager with testability enabled to generate NC faults. The
following figure displays how a not controlled input affects the output:
Figure 224

This section consists of the following topics:
* NC Analysis Method
* Running NC Analysis
* Configuration Fields in the Configuration File
* Generating and Loading Tracing Report in Verdi

NC Analysis Method
The current FDB organizes NC faults by their shared locations. You can further trace the
critical locations with NC faults to find the root cause that does not change value. This

manual debugging process is time-consuming and inefficient. The following figure displays
the unselected report that contains the blocking points with NC faults:
Figure 225

Unselected Report Format

Fault Ranking
The Fault Ranking utility automates to streamline debugging efforts. It focuses on blocking
points in the FDB that are caused from the same root cause, where the value does not
change. The automation reduces the redundant debugging.
The NC Fault Ranking utility scans all the critical locations with NC faults, It traces its fanin
cone until it finds no fanin or all fanin pins with changed values. In the NC Fault Ranking
report, a signal with no fanin or all fanin pins with the changed values is categorized as the
NC root cause. Critical locations are grouped based on the same root cause. The FDB NC
faults are grouped by the same critical location, and the critical locations are grouped by
the same root cause. All root causes that are formed by the same signal and module are
grouped together.
This automation minimizes manual debugging and traces NC signals directly to their root
causes, saving significant time and effort.
The following figure displays the NC fault ranking report:
Figure 226

NC Fault Ranking report

Tracing Behavior of NC Signal
The following are the rules to continue tracing the signals for NC critical locations:
* The input pins that are active (contributing to the output) and have a constant value are
circle.
marked with the red
* The input pins that are non-active (not contributing to the output) and have a constant
value are marked with the gray

circle.

* If all the input pins have

circle, expand the fanin pins.

* If a combination gate, for example, register and sequential gate, does not have an
active fanin value change, expand the non-active fanin pins.
The following rules, also called as the stop criteria, provide the exact root cause for NC
faults:
* If all fanin pin values change, tracing stops. The output is then marked as the root
cause.
* If the input signal has no driver, the signal is marked as the root cause.
* If all fanin pins of the non-combinational gates are non-active, the tracing stops. The
output is marked as the root cause.

Report Format
The FDB unselected report provides details about the traced location signals and their
associated faults. The report consists of the root causes, and each root cause has its
associated faults. The root causes are sorted based on the number of faults. You must
focus on the root causes to resolve the blocking points.

Figure 228

Report Format

For example, in Figure 228, consider the root-cause bucket (marked in the blue box)
consisting of the following details:
* ### Rootcauses Related to signal module.signal (1 rootcauses) combines
all the root causes belonging to the same module and signal.
* Root cause: signal name (xxx location ,xxx faults) displays the name of the
root cause, the number of locations, and the number of faults found in the locations. In
Figure 228, the test.a123.test_se signal covers 1727 locations and 2044 faults.
* Location provides the block point, similar to the block point in the Z01X unselected
report.
* NC 1 {PORT "signal name "} provides information of the NC fault, similar to the
Z01X unselected report.

Running NC Analysis
You can run the NC analysis using autorca.

To generate the configuration file template (run.yaml), use the following command:
autorca -gen_cfg_template <run.yaml> -gen_mode faultrca

When you run the command, the run.yaml file is generated.
The following are the requirements:
* The simv.daidir directory (required)
* The mode field must be set to 2 by default.
* The waveform is required for the NC Analysis.
For FDB, you must specify the following:
* FDB project name: Specify the name of the FDB project to be used.
* FDB path: Specify the full path of the FDB directory.
* Campaign name: Specify the campaign name that is used for dumping FDB.

Configuration Fields in the Configuration File
When you run the following command using autorca and gen_cfg_template, a
configuration file is generated:
autorca -gen_cfg_template <run.yaml> -gen_mode faultrca

You can use the autogenerated file (faultrca_report.xml) to run FaultRCA. For the
format of the file in the FaultRCA mode, refer to the Configuration File Format in FaultRCA
section.

For details about the other available fields, refer to the Configuration Fields in the

Limitation of FaultRCA

Limitation of FaultRCA
FaultRCA has the following limitation:
* FaultRCA does not support point-to-point trace in the nSchema feature for the symbollibrary setting mode.

The Not Controllable (NC) analysis provides a method to reduce manual efforts while
cleaning up the NC faults. NC faults occur in unselected signals during fault simulation.
An NC fault happens when the fanin value stays constant, which makes the fault
uncontrollable.
The existing FDB consists of multiple critical locations, and each critical location consists
of multiple faults. The faults are categorized with common location points to determine

NC Faults
NC faults are faults that stay constant during simulation. These faults occur when a signal,
which is the input to the fault, does not change its value. That is, the value stays at zero
or one throughout the simulation. The 0-X-0 or 1-X-1 state does not count as switching
states. You must run the fault manager with testability enabled to generate NC faults. The

NC Analysis Method
The current FDB organizes NC faults by their shared locations. You can further trace the
critical locations with NC faults to find the root cause that does not change value. This

manual debugging process is time-consuming and inefficient. The following figure displays
the unselected report that contains the blocking points with NC faults:
Figure 225

Unselected Report Format

Fault Ranking
The Fault Ranking utility automates to streamline debugging efforts. It focuses on blocking
points in the FDB that are caused from the same root cause, where the value does not
change. The automation reduces the redundant debugging.
The NC Fault Ranking utility scans all the critical locations with NC faults, It traces its fanin
cone until it finds no fanin or all fanin pins with changed values. In the NC Fault Ranking
report, a signal with no fanin or all fanin pins with the changed values is categorized as the
NC root cause. Critical locations are grouped based on the same root cause. The FDB NC
faults are grouped by the same critical location, and the critical locations are grouped by
the same root cause. All root causes that are formed by the same signal and module are
grouped together.
This automation minimizes manual debugging and traces NC signals directly to their root
causes, saving significant time and effort.

The FDB unselected report provides details about the traced location signals and their
associated faults. The report consists of the root causes, and each root cause has its
associated faults. The root causes are sorted based on the number of faults. You must
focus on the root causes to resolve the blocking points.

Running NC Analysis
You can run the NC analysis using autorca.

To generate the configuration file template (run.yaml), use the following command:
autorca -gen_cfg_template <run.yaml> -gen_mode faultrca

When you run the command, the run.yaml file is generated.
The following are the requirements:
* The simv.daidir directory (required)
* The mode field must be set to 2 by default.
* The waveform is required for the NC Analysis.
For FDB, you must specify the following:
* FDB project name: Specify the name of the FDB project to be used.
* FDB path: Specify the full path of the FDB directory.
* Campaign name: Specify the campaign name that is used for dumping FDB.

Configuration Fields in the Configuration File
When you run the following command using autorca and gen_cfg_template, a
configuration file is generated:
autorca -gen_cfg_template <run.yaml> -gen_mode faultrca

You can use the autogenerated file (faultrca_report.xml) to run FaultRCA. For the
format of the file in the FaultRCA mode, refer to the Configuration File Format in FaultRCA
section.
The following table describes the required fields in the configuration file:

Specify the Debug Mode
mode

Specify the debug mode. Set this field to 1
for the Fault Analysis mode and 2 for the NC
Fault Auto Ranking mode.
The default is 1.

Specify the path of the target debugging
database, simv.daidir.

target_waveform

Specify the target waveform file. It is a
required field for the Block Cell Detection
mode.

Fault Database Setting
fdb_project

Specify the name of the FDB project to be
used.

fdb_path

Specify the full path of the FDB directory.

campaign

Specify the fault campaign name.

For details about the other available fields, refer to the Configuration Fields in the
Configuration File section.

Generating and Loading Tracing Report in Verdi
You can generate the tracing report using the following autorca command:
autorca -cfg run.yaml

You can load the generated report in Verdi using the following command:
autorca -load_report faultrca_report.xml

Introduction
The Verdi(R) Automated Debug Platform and the Siloti(R) Visibility Automation System are
advanced solutions for debugging digital designs that increase design productivity with
complex System-on-Chip (SoC), ASIC, and FPGA designs.
The Verdi platform provides powerful technology to help you comprehend complex and
unfamiliar design behavior, automate difficult and tedious debug processes, unify diverse
and complicated design environments, and infer the dynamic behavior of a design over
time.
In addition to the standard features of a source code browser, schematics, waveforms,
state-machine diagrams, and waveform comparison (for comparing simulation results
in FSDB format), the Verdi platform includes advanced features for automatic tracing of
signal activity using temporal flow views, assertion-based debug, power-aware debug, and
debug and analysis of transaction and message data. All of this is available in a graphical
user interface using the Qt platform that supports multi-window docking and is easily
customizable.
The Siloti system speeds up the simulation by eliminating the overhead associated with
recording signal values and by enabling full visibility of the design activity based on a
relatively small amount of signal data captured during full-chip simulation, regression
simulation, and hardware emulation/ acceleration. The Siloti system is fully integrated with
the Verdi platform so that users can leverage the benefits of full visibility for gate or RTL
debug.
Synopsys also provides the following two modules that complement the Verdi platform:
* The nAnalyzer Design Analysis module is for debugging the implementation aspects of
the design, such as clock trees and static timing failures.
* The nECO Automated Netlist Modification module is for solving problems associated
with manual netlist changes.
The Verdi and Siloti systems and the additional nAnalyzer and nECO modules enable
engineers to locate, isolate, understand, and resolve bugs in a fraction of the time
of traditional solutions. This maximizes the efficiency and productivity of expensive
engineering resources, significantly reduces costs, and dramatically accelerates the
process of getting silicon to the market.

architectures.
* RHEL versions 7.3+ and 8+ are supported in the binary compatibility mode.

architectures.

* The 32-bit and 64-bit platforms both support the AMD Opteron and Intel EM64T
architectures.
* CentOS version 7.3.1611 is supported in the binary compatibility mode.

Availability of Verdi as a Single Linux Executable
Verdi is released as a Single Linux Executable (SLE). You can install Verdi only on Red
Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) platform and Verdi can run on SUSE operating system as a
binary compatible platform.
This change in the availability of Verdi as a SLE provides the following advantages:
* SLE is simple to install and use.
* Works with only one installation on Linux.

* Available as a single executable that works on various qualified Linux OS distributions.
* SLE ensures consistent product behavior on any Linux OS distribution.
You must install Verdi in an empty directory using the latest version of the Synopsys
Installer. Do not install this release over an existing release of a Synopsys tool.
Verdi uses the Synopsys Installer, which allows you to install the product using either
a text script or a graphical user interface (GUI). For information about downloading the
Synopsys Installer, see the Synopsys Installer section at the following address:
http://www.synopsys.com/install
To install Verdi, follow the procedures described in the Installing Synopsys Tools section.

Installation and Licensing Information
The Y-2026.03-SP2 release of the Verdi platform is a standalone release. It must be

Do not install this release over an existing release of Verdi or any Synopsys
tool.
Before running the Synopsys Tools, you must have installed and configured the Synopsys

file environment variable.
For detailed information about the SCL installation and setup, see the Synopsys Common
Licensing Quickstart Guide at the following address:
http://www.synopsys.com/licensing
This release of the product is based on Synopsys Common Licensing. You
must use the latest version of the SCL server (snpslmd daemon) and the
latest SCL license key file to use the product. For more information, see the

What's New in This Release
This section provides a brief description of the features introduced in the Y-2026.03-SP2
* Interactive Debug Feature
* Coverage Debug Features
* nWave Feature

Interactive Debug Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following Interactive Debug feature:
* Support for Virtual Interface Handles in Non-Component Class Objects

Support for Virtual Interface Handles in Non-Component Class
Objects
Starting with this release, Verdi introduces enhanced visibility for virtual interface handles
(VIFs) in the UVM Hierarchy Tree View. Verdi displays the VIFs that are direct members of
non-component class objects residing one level below the UVM components. This feature
is activated by enabling the +VERDI_DHIER_COMP_MEMBER_VIF simulation runtime option.
For more information, see "Interface Mapping Node in the OVM/UVM Hierarchy Tree" in
Verdi(R) UVM Debug User Guide.

What's New in This Release

Coverage Debug Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following Coverage Debug features:
* Covergroup Instance HVP Source Name Format Improvement
* Conversion Between XML Report and HVP
* Enhanced Plan Review
* Modifier Usability Enhancements
* Tcl Hook for Post-Recalculate Automation

Covergroup Instance HVP Source Name Format Improvement
Starting with this release, Verdi improves the source name format for covergroup
instances in the Hierarchical Verification Plan (HVP). When you define a covergroup
in a package, Verdi now uses only the full hierarchy path of the instance as the HVP
source name. The package name is no longer included as a prefix. This change ensures
unique and clear source names. It also simplifies source pattern definitions and improves
readability.
If you reuse the existing plans, Verdi maintains backward compatibility. You can still use
the previous source name format for matching.
For more information, see "HVP Source Name Format for Covergroup Instances" in the
Verdi Coverage User Guide and Tutorial.

Conversion Between XML Report and HVP
Starting with this release, Verdi supports converting between XML report and Hierarchical
Verification Plan (HVP) formats. You can save and load expanded XML reports in both file
mode and VMS mode, making integration with HVP and Verdi coverage seamless. This
enhancement improves report readability and enables round-trip usage between Verdi
coverage and HVP flows.
For more information, see "Generating the HVP Excel XML Plan With Report" in the Verdi
Coverage User Guide and Tutorial.

Enhanced Plan Review
Starting with this release, Verdi improves plan review usability in the GUI. Plans now
open in an expanded state by default, showing first-level features and subplans for faster
navigation. You can use new and enhanced context menu options and keyboard shortcuts
to expand or collapse plan nodes by feature, measure, or source level. The Plan view
adds an optional Source Patterns column to display source information at the measure
level, supporting multiline and wrapped text. These changes make plan review more
efficient and configurable.

What's New in This Release

For more information, see "Using the HVP Planner" in the Verdi Coverage User Guide and
Tutorial.

Modifier Usability Enhancements
Starting with this release, Verdi displays clear indicators when modifiers are applied to a
plan, even if the modifier window is closed. You can also view invalid operands in modifier
expressions and see the applied status, including matched counts and modified item
names. You can also activate or deactivate all child modifiers at once using the master
check box for a modifier file. These enhancements simplify modifier management and
improve workflow transparency.
For more information, see "Using Modifiers" in the Verdi Coverage User Guide and
Tutorial.

Tcl Hook for Post-Recalculate Automation
Starting with this release, Verdi supports a Tcl hook framework that allows you to register
Tcl procs to run automatically after each Hierarchical Verification Plan (HVP) recalculate.
This feature enables seamless automation and custom workflows triggered by recalculate
completion. Use the bundled reference proc or create your own to streamline verification
plan management and improve efficiency.
For more information, see "Post-Recalculate Hook Framework" in the Verdi Coverage
User Guide and Tutorial and the "Coverage Debug" chapter in the Verdi and Siloti Tcl
Reference.

Enhanced Signal Addition with Index Wildcards in nWave
Starting with this release, nWave supports wildcard characters in array indices when
adding signals through the Add Signal by Name dialog box. This enhancement simplifies
signal selection by allowing users to specify patterns that match multiple indexed signals,
eliminating the need to enter each signal individually. When a wildcard pattern is entered,

VIA Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following VIA feature:
* Module Parameter Insight Report

Module Parameter Insight Report
Get Module Parameter is a design-comprehension feature used to report module
parameter values across the design hierarchy, helping users quickly understand how
parameterized instances are configured during debug, analysis, and review.
In earlier releases, mode supported only default, local, type, and other. In Y-2026.03SP-1, a new mode, non-local, is added to report only the non-local parameters.
The updated mode definitions are as follows:
default: dump all kinds of parameters
local: only dump local parameters

Available Features in the Y-2026.03-SP1 Release

type: only dump type parameters
other: only dump non-local and non-type parameters
non-local: only dump non-local parameters

Coverage Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following Coverage features:
* Auto-Export of Sub-Plans When Syncing Top Plan
* RM Link Synchronization Through a CLI Option

Auto-Export of Sub-Plans When Syncing Top Plan
Starting with this release, the Verdi tool supports automatic export of all sub-plans when
you export a top plan to Jama. You no longer need to export each sub-plan manually.
This feature reduces errors and saves time, especially for large plans. Control autoexport using the ENABLE_NEW_RM_MANAGER and AUTO_SYNC_SUBPLAN_MODE environment
variables. The tool always syncs sub-plans automatically on the first export. For
incremental syncs, you must select the Accept SubPlan checkbox in the RM Review
Window.

RM Link Synchronization Through a CLI Option
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the -sync_rm_link <0|1> command-line option.
This option allows you to force the RM Link Synchronization preference on or off for the
current session, overriding the value in novas.rc. Use this feature to ensure consistent
behavior in automated and batch flows, regardless of user or host settings.

Available Features in the Y-2026.03-SP1 Release
This section provides a brief description of the features introduced in the Y-2026.03-SP1
* Regression Debug Automation Feature

Available Features in the Y-2026.03-SP1 Release

Regression Debug Automation Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following Regression Debug Automation
(RDA) feature:
* XRCA Timing Violation Correlation

XRCA Timing Violation Correlation
XRCA automatically correlates X root causes with timing-violation messages in the
simulation log. Matching root causes are annotated with the reason "X from timing
violation." You can navigate directly to the relevant log line in SmartLog or to the
corresponding source location.
For more details, refer to "XRCA Timing Violation Correlation" in the Regression Debug
Automation (RDA) User Guide.

Coverage Debug Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following Coverage Debug features:
* Support for User-Defined Attribute Values for Measures
* GUI Updates in the Save Plan As Dialog Box
* Support for the Use of Current HVP Plan in Older Verdi Releases
* Support for Viewing Plan Metadata
* Naming of HVP Plan Items

Support for User-Defined Attribute Values for Measures
With this release, you can assign the values of user defined attributes for measures in an
HVP file. All attributes defined at the plan level can be edited for measures in Verdi HVP
and HVP detailed views.
In file-based mode, you can edit or revert these user-defined attribute values at the
measure level in Verdi coverage. These can be exported and imported back on Verdi
coverage. The Save Plan As(Backward Compatible) command enables saving the user
defined attributes for measures.

GUI Updates in the Save Plan As Dialog Box
Staring with this release, the -merge_measures options field in the Save Plan As dialog
box of the Verdi Coverage GUI has been renamed as Additional Options.
For more information on this option, see "Saving the Plan" in Chapter 5, "Using Verification
Planner", in the Verdi(R) Coverage User Guide and Tutorial.

Available Features in the Y-2026.03-SP1 Release

Support for the Use of Current HVP Plan in Older Verdi Releases
Starting with this release, the Save Plan As (Backward compatible) option in the Verdi
Coverage GUI has been renamed as Save Plan As Older Version, and this option has
been moved to the end of the Plan drop-down menu. You can use this option to export
your current HVP plan to use in older Verdi releases.
For more details on the Save Plan As Older Version option, see "Saving the Plan" in
Chapter 5, "Using Verification Planner", in the Verdi(R) Coverage User Guide and Tutorial.

Support for Viewing Plan Metadata
Starting with this release, saved plan files record the save-time metadata so that you
can see which HVP or plan build produced a file, which tool wrote it, and what options
were used. You can view the metadata of the saved files in Verdi, URG, hvpexport, HVP
utilities (Doc Plan Generator or HVP gendoc, HVP genxls, HVP annotate), HVP dump, and
reports.
For more details about viewing plan metadata, see "Viewing Plan Metadata" in Chapter 5,
"Using Verification Planner", in the Verdi(R) Coverage User Guide and Tutorial and Chapter
1, "Verification Planner", in the Verification Planner User Guide.

Available Features in the Y-2026.03-1 Release

nWave Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following nWave feature:

Enhanced Signal Addition with Index Wildcards in nWave
Starting with this release, nWave supports wildcard characters in array indices when
adding signals through the Add Signal by Name dialog box. This enhancement simplifies
signal selection by allowing users to specify patterns that match multiple indexed signals,
eliminating the need to enter each signal individually. When a wildcard pattern is entered,
nWave automatically expands the matching entries and adds the corresponding signals to
the waveform viewer.
For more details, refer to "Adding Signals Using Index Wildcards" in the Verdi User Guide
and Tutorial.

HW/SW Debug Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following HW/SW debug feature:
* Merging gcov JSON Coverage with HW/SW Debug Coverage

Merging gcov JSON Coverage with HW/SW Debug Coverage
Verdi now supports a direct, interactive workflow by allowing you to ingest software
coverage data directly into the coverage database (covdb). You can merge software unit
line coverage generated by gcov with source-level line coverage generated by HW/SW
Debug.

Available Features in the Y-2026.03-1 Release
This section provides a brief description of the features introduced in the Y-2026.03-1
* AMS Feature
* VIA Feature

AMS Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following AMS enhancement:
* Bus IE Alias and Array Data Type Support

Bus IE Alias and Array Data Type Support
Verdi adds support for dumping bus Interface Element (IE) aliases with the IE_All option.
It also adds array data type support in the analog view.
You can debug analog signals alongside their digital bus signals. This improves visibility
and analysis at the analog-digital boundary.
Enhanced array support also streamlines array handling and signal management.
To enable this feature, set the following environment variable:
setenv FSDB_IE_ALL_ANALOG_BUS

Use the dumping command with the required options:
fsdbDumpvars 0 +IE_All +msv+v

VIA Feature
Stating with this release, Verdi supports the following VIA enhancement:

Support for the Escape Symbol before '.' in Hierarchical Path
Component Names
Support is now available for the backslash \ (escape) symbol before the dot . in
hierarchical path component names. This includes scope or instance names and the leaf
signal name.
In earlier releases, you could not retrieve signals that used the escape symbol, even when
the signal name appeared in the Native Programming Interface (NPI). You can now access
signals that include this format.
Example
\ADC.AFE0.afe_diff\.pc\.amp_dual\.ampn\.ibnmch

The example signal definition can be retrieved by using npi_fsdb_sig_property_str.
However, by using npi_fsdb_sig_by_name, the API returns null.

PureLog Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following PureLog feature:
* Timing Violation Summary Report

Timing Violation Summary Report
The PureLog timing violation solution helps you to resolve timing violations more
intelligently and efficiently.
The major features are as follows:
* Summarize the timing violations based on components.
Easy to dispatch task to the right owner.
* Prioritize timing violations in different scenarios wherein, you can pick the best one for
the particular scenario.
The corrupted flip-flop with the higher number of violations.
Active drivers associated with a higher number of violations.
* Support waive or unwaive operations effectively.
Waive conditions are saved or restored for the next run.
All waiver justifications are logged into the database for projectlevel review.
* Enable rapid debug workflows for timing violation analysis

Oneclick access to related signals, violation messages in the simulation log, and
TFV trace results.
For more information, see "Timing Violation Summary Report" section in the Verdi(R)
and Siloti(R) LCA Features Guide.

text:
Python-Based NPI CRDB Model
The Python-Based NPI CRDB (Correlation Database) Model helps users to check and
query how scopes and signals are mapped between RTL and gate-level designs.
This feature makes it easier to understand the relationship between different design levels.
For more information, see the Verdi(R) Python-Based NPI CRDB Model Guide.

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
DDT External Link Tree
DDT offers a feature called External Link. With External Link, you can link other DDT
sessions to their current DDT, similar to a soft link in a file system.
Also, starting with this release, DDT offers new GUI features. These include Pan Mode
and Selection Mode, User-Defined Node Properties, Plugin, Multi Parent (Topological)
Mode, Selective Run, Customize Python Library, and Available Commands.
Available Commands include add_external_link_session,
delete_external_link_session, and update_external_link_session.
For more information, see the Verdi(R) Debug Decision Tree User Guide.

nSchema Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following nSchema feature:
* ViewMark Manager Pane for nSchema

ViewMark Manager Pane for nSchema
Starting with this release, the Verdi tool adds the ViewMark Manager pane in the
nSchema window. This pane enables easy saving and loading of schematic views using
simple Save View and Load View buttons with a file browser dialog box.

For more information, see "Schematic Commands" section in "nSchema" chapter of the
Verdi(R) and Siloti(R) Command Reference Guide and "nSchema" chapter of the Verdi Tcl
Reference Guide.

nTrace Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following nTrace features:
* Array Index Increment/Decrement in Source Code Annotation
* Non-Blocking Find Dialog Box for Scope, Signal, and Instance
* Ability to Analyze Simulation Loop Data

Array Index Increment/Decrement in Source Code Annotation
Starting with this release, the Verdi tool allows you to easily change the array index value
for source code annotation using new increment and decrement options in the Specify
Index Value of Array dialog box.
For more information, see "Support for Special Array Index" section in "nTrace Tutorial"
chapter in the Verdi(R) User Guide and Tutorial.

Non-Blocking Find Dialog Box for Scope, Signal, and Instance
Starting with this release, Verdi introduces non-blocking FindScope, FindSignal, and
FindInstance dialog boxes.
These dialog boxes search in the background. You can continue working in other windows
while they run, even with designs that have large numbers of instances or signals.
For more information, see "Source Commands" section in the "nTrace" chapter in the
Verdi(R) and Siloti(R) Command Reference Guide.

Ability to Analyze Simulation Loop Data
Sometimes a simulation loop causes the simulation to freeze. Signals may also show
abnormal glitch counts.
Verdi can detect and report these issues using FSDB data captured with the -
loopdbg_dir option.
To analyze the simulation loop data, you must choose the work directory through File >
Analyze Simulation Loop Data in nTrace.
Verdi identifies critical paths related to freeze issues and displays them in a table.
You can view full or partial loop paths and inspect all signals involved.

You can also visualize problematic paths in TFV and nSchema windows and save
detected paths for later review.
This feature helps you diagnose and resolve simulation freeze problems. It helps you
pinpoint and fix design issues faster.
For more information, see "Analyze Simulation Loop Data" in Verdi and Siloti Command
Reference.

AMS Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following AMS feature:
* RTVS Features License Expansion

RTVS Features License Expansion
Verdi enables Real-Time View Swapping (RTVS) features with Verdi Elite (verdi -elite)
as well as Verdi Apex (verdi -apex) licenses.
This update provides greater flexibility and ensures seamless access to RTVS functionality
across supported license tiers.

GUI/QT Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following GUI/QT features:
* Unified Filter in Verdi
* EDR Serverless Mode
* Launch Application in nTrace Tool Commands

Unified Filter in Verdi
The Unified Filter provides several improvements that make searching and filtering more
consistent and intuitive across Verdi. These enhancements streamline preference options
and align the behaviors of Find and Filter features for a smoother user experience. Key
enhancements include merged Find/Filter preference settings, updated default filtering
behavior for case-insensitive and partial match, and improved consistency between Find
and Filter operations.
For more information, see the Verdi(R) Command Reference Guide.

EDR Serverless Mode
EDR Serverless Mode allows you to save and replay EDR sessions locally, without
needing a server. This is useful for users who have limited access to server resources or
want to keep debug data on their own machine.
For more information, see "EDR Serverless Mode" section in the Verdi(R) and Siloti(R) LCA
Features Guide.

Launch Application in nTrace Tool Commands
The following nTrace Tool commands are now grouped under Launch Applications
menu.
* Invoke HW/SW Debug
* DDT
* Coverage
* VMS Planner
* VMS (ExecMan)
* Save Electronic Debug Record
* Browse Electronic Debug Record
For more information, see "Launch Applications" section in the Verdi(R) Command
Reference Guide.

nWave Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following nWave features:
* Adjustable Find Bar
* Displaying the Scope and Signal Statistical Data
* Pasting Signal Full Hierarchy in Get Signals Form Scope Search

Adjustable Find Bar
Starting with this release, you can resize the find bar by dragging its handle left or right.
The direction depends on its alignment in the window.
This makes search more convenient and tailored to your workflow. The find bar appears in
each docking window, so you can search multiple panes at the same time.
Open the find bar with Ctrl+F. Close it with ESC or the X icon.

Search options include Match Case, Wildcard, Regex, and Whole Words Match.
To use the original fixed-width find bar, set the environment variable
VERDI_DISABLE_UNIFIND_BAR_RESIZE to disable resizing.

Displaying the Scope and Signal Statistical Data
The Signal List Pane also displays the number of scopes and signals at the bottom of the

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
ginal fixed-width find bar, set the environment variable
VERDI_DISABLE_UNIFIND_BAR_RESIZE to disable resizing.

Displaying the Scope and Signal Statistical Data
The Signal List Pane also displays the number of scopes and signals at the bottom of the
scope/signal list. This helps you quickly understand the size of your design and manage
signal selection more efficiently.
For more information, see "Get Signals" section in the Verdi(R) Command Reference Guide.

Pasting Signal Full Hierarchy in Get Signals Form Scope Search
You can quickly locate and select signals in the Get Signals form by pasting their full
hierarchical names. This feature helps you find signals faster, especially in large designs,
by jumping directly to the parent scope and highlighting the signal if it exists.
For more information, see "Get Signals" section in the Verdi(R) Command Reference Guide.

RDA Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following enhancements in RDA:
* Reusing Design Change Report
* Assigning Bucket and Tracking Status in RCA Manager

Reusing Design Change Report
The tool can automatically compare two versions of a design and generate a detailed
report of the differences. This helps you instantly identify what has changed. It allows you
to find the root cause of new issues much faster and simplify regression analysis.
For more details about the design_change_info_path option, see "Configuration Fields
in the Configuration File" in Chapter 6, "DUT Root Cause Analysis (DUTRCA)," in the
Regression Debug Automation (RDA) User Guide.

Assigning Bucket and Tracking Status in RCA Manager
RDA introduces bucket assignment and status tracking in the RCA Manager for regression
binning. You can assign buckets to enrolled users, track their status, and manage
assignee directly from the RCA Manager interface. This feature streamlines collaboration,
ensures clear ownership, and improves accountability during debugging. Database
configuration in the YAML file enables persistent tracking and management of bucket
assignments.

For more details on assigning and managing bucket, see "Assigning And Managing
Bucket" in Chapter 3, "Regression Binning," in the Regression Debug Automation (RDA)
User Guide.

Fault Analysis Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following Fault Analysis feature:
* Ability to Configure the Generation of YAML and FSDB Files

Ability to Configure the Generation of YAML and FSDB Files
The VerdiFA tool can automatically generate YAML files compatible with FaultRCA. You
can enable this when generating GMFM FSDB files for supported fault types (st@0 and
st@1).
This feature helps you set up FaultRCA analysis quickly. It speeds up root cause
identification and improves debug efficiency.
Verdi also lets you control the FSDB database type using the fault simulation mode.
In concurrent FSim mode, you can configure whether the FSDB has both faulty and faultfree results (GM+FM) or only faulty results (FM only).
In serial FSim mode, you can generate an FSDB with faulty results only.
For more information, see "Generating Data for Fault Analysis in the FaultDetail Window"
in the VerdiFault Analysis and Debug User Guide.

FSDB/Dumper Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following FSDB/Dumper feature:
* Support for Dumping Assertion Disable Status
* Ability to Analyze Simulation Loop Data

Support for Dumping Assertion Disable Status
Verdi supports both the following runtime option and environment variable to dump the
assertion disable status:
* +fsdb+sva_disable_status
* setenv FSDB_SVA_DISABLE_STATUS 1

* Verdi must also use the following runtime option or environment variable to
enable this feature:
+fsdb+sva_status
or
setenv FSDB_SVA_STATUS 1
* This option is supported only with VCS simulator (VCS 2025.06-SP2 and
newer versions).
* For VCS 2025.06, it requires VCS

-debug_perf=fsdb_sva_disable_status compile option to enable this

feature.

* The FSDB version is upgraded to 6.7 if you specify the options to enable
this feature. It requires the newest Verdi to read the FSDB.

Ability to Analyze Simulation Loop Data
Sometimes a simulation loop causes the simulation to freeze. Signals may also show
abnormal glitch counts.
Verdi can detect and report these issues using FSDB data captured with the -
loopdbg_dir option.
To analyze the simulation loop data, you must choose the work directory through File >
Analyze Simulation Loop Datain nTRace.
Verdi identifies critical paths related to freeze issues and displays them in a table.
You can view full or partial loop paths and inspect all signals involved.
You can also visualize problematic paths in TFV and nSchema windows and save
detected paths for later review.
This feature helps you diagnose and resolve simulation freeze problems. It helps you
pinpoint and fix design issues faster.
For more information, see "Analyze Simulation Loop Data" in Verdi and Siloti Command
Reference.

Compiler Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following Compiler enhancement:
* Making Verdi KDB Elaboration Database Self-Contained Using -kdb=selfcontained

Making Verdi KDB Elaboration Database Self-Contained Using
-kdb=selfcontained
The -kdb=selfcontained option in VCS helps you create a self-contained Verdi
Knowledge Database (KDB) during the 3-step compilation flow. By default, the KDB
directory contains symbolic links to files in physical libraries outside the KDB directory.
This can cause problems if you want to move or copy the KDB to another location, such
as a different server or cloud storage. Using this option, you can replace these links with
actual files, making the KDB directory fully portable.
For more information, see "Making Verdi KDB Elaboration Database Self-Contained Using
-kdb=selfcontained" in the "Launching Techniques" in the Verdi User Guide and Tutorial.

DesignDiff Feature
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following DesignDiff enhancement:
* Supporting Process or Unnamed Block Mapping

Supporting Process or Unnamed Block Mapping
Starting with this release, Verdi introduces a concept for process or unnamed block
mapping in the DesignDiff feature. The tool excludes all unnamed blocks that are not
changed. It performs a comprehensive comparison between reference and target always
blocks, considering all possible combinations. The mapping prioritizes block content--
such as assignment changes, branch counts, and condition changes--over sensitivity
lists. This ensures that the most relevant differences are highlighted.

Available LCA Features in the Y-2026.03-1 Release

Verdi ICO Features
Starting with this release, Verdi supports the following Verdi ICO enhancements:
* Intelligent Constraint Debugger
* The Intelligent Simulation Replayer

Intelligent Constraint Debugger
Finding the root cause of the test failures such as UVM_ERROR, SVA failures, checker
failure, and so on is laborious and requires several trial-error cycles that slow down the
entire verification process and make it harder to achieve verification closure in a timely
manner.
The Intelligent Constraint Debugger (ICD) feature allows you to automate the localization
of the failure-inducing randomization constraints and reduces the manual debugging effort.

The Intelligent Simulation Replayer
The Intelligent Simulation Replayer (ISR) helps to replay a simulation in a best-effort
case considering design/testbench changes. The resimulation allows you to match the
generated stimulus values modulo TB changes. This feature helps to reproduce rare
observations such as failures in the modified TB.
For more details, refer to the Verdi and Siloti LCA Features Guide.

Verdi Assistant
Verdi Assistant is an AI-powered feature that integrates a Large Language Model (LLM)
into the Verdi environment. It provides a chatbot interface for conversational debugging.
This feature allows you to interact with Verdi by using natural language. As a result, you
can find commands, execute them, obtain documentation or answers to usage questions
easily. Verdi Assistant automates command execution and provides instant support. It
reduces the learning curve for new users and increases productivity of experienced users.
For more details, refer to the Verdi Assistant chapter in the Verdi and Siloti LCA Features
Guide.

Ability to Check Message Protocols
Starting to debug by checking the message protocol narrows down the debug scope.
Message protocol debugging can be done through both GUI and batch modes. PureLog
supports specifying as well as checking protocols. See Message Protocol section in the
Verdi(R) and Siloti(R) LCA Features Guide for more information.

Support for Multile SmartSheets for Cross Reference of Multiple
Log Sets
Purelog enables users to open two log sets in different SmartSheet windows but visualize
them in one nWave window. For more information, see Visualization View section in the
Verdi(R) and Siloti(R) LCA Features Guide.

Ability to Bind Design Signals to Log Messages
PureLog can visualize log messages in event/transaction/signal terms without rerunning
a simulation. In some cases, debugging is based on log message signals along with the
real fsdb signals generated from a simulation. Users can now specify dumped signals
related to log message signals as part of a one-time activity. As a result, when any user
visualizes log message signals, eventually, the related binding dumped signals show up
automatically. For more information, see Bind Design Signals to Log Message section in
the Verdi(R) and Siloti(R) LCA Features Guide.

Availability of Internal Partition Rules for VCS Logs
PureLog provides internal partition rules for VCS logs including compile- and run-time
logs. Users can apply these internal rules both in file-based and DB-based debugging.
For more information, see Setting the Column Filter section in the Verdi User Guide and
Tutorial.

Support Scientific Notations for Real Metric Values in the HVP
View
Starting with this release, the Verdi HVP view supports Scientific notation with 'e' notation
and SI Prefixes for the sim_min and sim_max values. That is, the expression `e' and unit
are now supported for the real metric values in the HVP view.

WaveCheck to enable users to check signals (analog and digital) in FSDB/Waveform files
based on the requirement.
WaveCheck has the following modules to check analog and digital values of MSV(Mix
Signal Validation) simulations without collateral modifications by using WaveCheck utility:
* WaveCheck Entry
* Checker Command Keywords

Support for Changing Fonts
Verdi Coverage supports changing the font and the font size globally. You can edit the
application font and the monospaced font. The application font applies to the menu bar,
toolbar, dialog boxes, and all Coverage views except those where the monospaced font is
applied. The monospaced font applies to the content in the source view.

Python Interface for Verdi
Python interface allows you to execute Python inside Verdi by providing a wrapper
that wraps the current Tcl command interface in GUI. To enable this feature, set the
VERDI_ENABLE_PYTHON_INTERFACE environment variable.
For more information on this feature, see Python Interface for Verdi section in the Verdi
and Siloti LCA Features Guide.

Verdi Formal Navigator
You can now leverage the Navigator feature of VC Formal in Verdi for waveform
manipulation, plotting, and design exploration, without requiring detailed knowledge of

how to use the complete VC Formal tool. You can edit the signal values in a waveform
cycle-by-cycle, plot the waveform again, and generate a new scenario, or extend the
current waveform for additional cycles. You can also experiment with different verification
scenarios without changing the testbench and recompiling to run the simulation again.
For more information on this feature, see the Verdi Formal Navigator section in the Verdi
and Siloti LCA Features Guide.

Dumping Queue, Dynamic Array, and Associative Array in HDL
Instance
You can enable the dumping of non-static array (queue, dynamic array, and associative
array) in HDL instance using the following options.
Use Model
+fsdb+variant_size_array

This option enables dumping for the non-static arrays in HDL instances, such as dynamic
array, queue, and associative array. As the array size can be big, FSDB dumper only
dumps several array elements in a non-static arrays. The default number is 10 and the
array element starts from index 0.
+fsdb+variant_size_array

This option specifies the different element numbers of non-static arrays. The number must
be 0 ~ 1023.
For more information, refer to Verdi LCA Features Guide.

Specifying FSDB File Name for UVM Enabled Features
By default, UVM data is dumped into the default FSDB file. You can use the
+uvm_fsdbfile=<filename.fsdb> runtime option to specify the FSDB file for the UVM

For details about this feature, see the UVM Aware Debug chapter in the Verdi and Siloti
LCA Features Guide.

Unified Transaction and Signal Waveform Debugging in nWave
This feature enables you to add both transactions and signals into nWave. Thus, the
integrated nWave window helps you get the maximum benefit of the screen size and other
features to debug an error using both transactions and waveforms on a single application
window.
For details about this feature, see the Transaction Debug chapter in the Verdi and Siloti
LCA Features Guide.

Mark Transaction in Protocol Analyzer Window
This feature enables you to mark transactions in the Transaction and Protocol Analyzer
window so that you can come back to the marked transaction easily even if other
transactions are selected.
For details about this feature, see the Transaction Debug chapter in the Verdi and Siloti
LCA Features Guide.

Support for Static Bug Finding Root Cause Analysis (SBRCA) in
RDA
RDA provides a Static Bug Finding Root Cause Analysis (SBRCA) solution that
automatically groups violations into a lower number of groups and provides connections to
further debug with waveform, source code, and simulation log and uses Verdi for debug.
For more details about this feature, refer to the Static Bug Finding Root Cause Analysis
(SBRCA) section in the Regression Debug Automation (RDA) chapter of the Verdi and
Siloti LCA Features Guide.

RDA Integration With VC Execution Manager (ExecMan) in RDA
Once the RDA is enabled, the RDA integration with VC Execution Manager (ExecMan)
feature allows applying incremental binning to parallel debug by default. The ExecMan
feature, Parallel debug, allows running debug tests immediately after the test fails in its
custom failure category. Incremental binning categorizes tests one by one and supports
the ExecMan Parallel Debug feature.
For more details about this feature, refer to the RDA Integration With VC Execution
Manager (ExecMan) section in the Regression Debug Automation (RDA) chapter of the
Verdi and Siloti LCA Features Guide.

PureLog
PureLog is a log-based debug platform that has many utilities to speed up the debug
cycle, such as Log Navigator (SmartLog), Log Tracer, Register Map, Log- to-Wave,
PureLog Database (PureLog DB), DB Debug Platform, Abnormal Analysis, and Sheet
Navigator (SmartSheet).
For details about these features, see the PureLog chapter in the Verdi and Siloti LCA
Features Guide.

Waveutils --tool=2saif Utility Supports Multi- threads
The -thread_number n option is used to specify the thread numbers to convert SAIF
file, n is the number of threads; it can be 1 to 4. By default, multi- thread is enabled with
waveutils --tool=2saif utility, the default thread number is 4.
For more information on this feature, see Verdi and Siloti LCA Features Guide.

Electronic Debug Feature (EDR)
In the EDR feature, the debug sessions are stored on a database. You may search and
load the debug notes without any transfer of local files.
For details about this feature, see the Electronic Debug Record (EDR) chapter in the Verdi
and Siloti LCA Features Guide.

Next Generation Debug GUI
Verdi enhances the look and feel of the GUI by providing the following customized NextGeneration GUI features:
* Color Themes
* Grid and Density
* Banners
* Search

* Find
* Quick Launcher
* Recently Used Command Buttons
* Toolbar With Text and Icon
For more information on this feature, see Verdi and Siloti LCA Features Guide.

Third-Party Simulators
Synopsys supports some third-party simulators' ability to output FSDB. Synopsys validates
the flows as expeditiously as possible. However, there maybe circumstances outside of
our control due to third party vendors' release timelines and their timely communications
to Synopsys. When this situation arises, you may see a warning message. The warning
is removed after we receive the required notification and materials from the third party
vendor, and we are able to re-validate the flow.

New Supported Simulators
Verdi Y-2026.03-SP2 is compatible with the following third-party simulators:
* Xcelium 2025.03
* Xcelium 2024.09
* Xcelium 2023.09
* Xcelium 2023.03
* Xcelium 2022.09
* Xcelium 2022.03
* Xcelium 2021.09
* Questa 2023.x (includes Questa 2023.1 ~ Questa 2023.4)

Known Problems and Limitations
This chapter describes limitations and known issues in the Verdi Y-2026.03-SP2 release. A
workaround may be provided under each limitation.
* DesignDiff
* QT4 to QT5 Migration
* Port Expressions

* SystemVerilog/SVA/SVTB Language Support

* FSDB and Essential Signal Dumping
* Tcl/Tk Interface

* Limitations of Data Expansion

DesignDiff
DesignDiff has the following limitation:
* DesignDiff only maps blocks at the process level (initial, always, final). When
multiple sequential blocks (begin/end) exist within the same process, DesignDiff does
not map these sibling blocks individually. Differences might be reported incorrectly or
additional differences might appear.
This limitation affects cases where you expect mapping for sibling sequential blocks
inside a single process. To achieve correct mapping, place each sequential block in a
separate process (for example, use separate initial begin end blocks).
For more information, refer to the DesignDiff chapter of the Verdi and Siloti LCA Features
Guide.

QT4 to QT5 Migration
Verdi GUI uses the QT5 framework for enhanced usability, which requires an additional
~300MB than the QT4 framework.

Port Expressions
Bit-select and part-select arrays in port expressions in the module header are not
supported.

License Check after Idle Verdi
If the NOVAS_IDLE_LICENSE_CHECKBACK environment variable is enabled and the license
is released after the specified idle time, there might be some delays in the GUI operation.
The delay is decided based on the network communication between license nodes.

Coverage has the following limitations:

Font Display

When multiple HVP files are open with specification linking features, the embedded PDF

Propagation
*

Macro support depends on the user's response.
The include file in if-else or case statement is not supported.
If xprop.log has multi-instruments in the same line, only the first instrument is
recognized.
As xprop.log records relative file names, in order to find the correct file, the design
needs to be compiled in the same path for Verdi and VCS.

Protected Code

Only the command line can be used to input the xprop.log file. To change the
xprop.log file, the command needs to be entered again.
Both begin and end values are considered in a value change time. This is because
the FSDB file only records these two values and does not record the time at which
the value changes. In the following example, "a" and "b" are both x when the case is
executed. If only the latest value is used, "a" and "b" are both 0, and which is wrong.
This issue only happens in always@(clk) and not in always_comb condition.
always@(posedge clk) begin case(1'b1)
a: y=2'b00; // a = x to 0 b: y=2'b01; // b = x to 0
default: y=2'b0z;
endcase a=0; b=0;
end
initial begin a=1'bx; b=1'bx; clk=0;
# 1;
clk=1;
end

*

not be completely correct.

fsdbextract and fsdbmerge utilities is not supported.

*

If a variable is forced or released by the statement and UCLI command at the same

Tracing results for the active drivers of a variable include all of the statements

If an array or a slice of an array is forced from a UCLI command, nTrace

only returns one external command as the tracing result.

In nWave, displaying forced information for runtime signals is not supported.
In nWave, displaying the forced glitch in expand mode is not supported.

Siloti

Siloti
This section describes known problems and limitations for Siloti functions.

Behavior Analysis
*

Data Expansion needs Behavior Analysis to flatten all arrays in order to perform
computation correctly. This requires the FLAT_ALL_ARRAYS environment variable to
be set to 1, before running Verdi/Siloti. The default value of FLAT_ALL_ARRAYS is 0.
The recommended Siloti flow suggests FLAT_ALL_ARRAYS value be in sync between
ESA and DE, and preferably both set to 1.
The Behavior Database (BDB) and on-the-fly Behavior Analysis (BA) are mutually
exclusive.
After loading in the BDB, if you want to change the Behavior Analysis scope (BA,
TFV), the BDB is thrown away and BA is re-run from the start.

Essential Signal Analysis
*

Signals driving a clock signal through a sequential element are not recognized as
high-frequency signals.
Even if a sub-field of a signal is recognized as a high-frequency signal, the signal
itself is not recognized as high-frequency.
ESA does not recognize statements with delay in VHDL as essential signals.
Auto variables cannot be dumped into the FSDB. Therefore, if an auto variable is
considered an essential signal, ESA includes the signals driven by the auto variable
in the essential signal database.

Essential Signal Dumping
*

The +parameter, +strength and +Reg_Only options of the

$fsdbDumpvars dumping command are not supported in the ES dumping flow.

*

$fsdbSuppress does not work on signals with essential signal dumping. It only
works at the module and the instance level.

Siloti

Data Expansion
*

Data Expansion has limited modport expression support in terms of assignment
pattern expression.
Currently, VCS does not support assignment pattern expressions specified
in modport expressions connected to the output mpport. Therefore, Data
Expansion cannot compute the modport expression results in this scenario.
Data Expansion has limited modport expression supports in terms of multidimensional arrays.
Mpports and references to an interface item of a modport instance cannot
be created/computed by Data Expansion and is displayed as `NF' for Active
Annotation.
Data Expansion computes properly for

Interface_instance.Modport_name.Mpport_name that can be accessed from

the Get Signals form in nWave.

For computed VHDL enum signals, Siloti may insert `NV' or `NC' into the string
table. If you also use `NV' or `NC' as an enum string value, you would not be able to
identify the real `NV' or `NC' state from the original definition.
Data Expansion does not calculate values for signals inside functions and tasks.
For functions, use the Siloti/Verdi function debug capability. For tasks, confirm that
the Include Signals in Tasks option is enabled during ESA.
Data Expansion does not support VHDL physical types (for example, TIME type).
If a physical type is not dumped to the FSDB file specifically, it shows NC for noncomputable signals.
Data Expansion does not calculate the following VHDL data objects/types:
Variable
String
Signals outside the Essential Signal Analysis working scope are not expandable.
If the loaded design and Behavior Analysis options are different between Essential
Signal Analysis and Data Expansion, for example, different working scopes or
missing modules, some signals may not be expandable.
Data Expansion may not be able to expand a signal if the essential signals within its
fan-in cone are excluded by any of the Essential Signal Analysis exclude options.
Data Expansion does not calculate values for signals that are automatic variables.
There is an Essential Signal Analysis option to dump variables as essential signals.

Siloti

Data Expansion is a functional simulation and is cycle-based. It does not compute
delays and glitches.
There is a DE limitation on initial value mismatches. This is due to the evaluation
of simulators that is triggered by the sensitivity list of the RTL model. However, DE
synthesizes the design into the gate-level model, and the evaluation is triggered by
any of the signals in the gate-level model's fan-in cone. The simulator's sensitivity
list and DE's gate-level model fan-in cone may be different causing a mismatched
value that is often found in the initial time. These types of mismatched signals are
identified and can be dumped to the ESA list by setting an environment variable
(setenv ESA_DE_INIT_MISMATCH 1). This includes a trade-off that when more
delay signals are dumped to the ESA list, the size of the resulting ESA FSDB dump
files is bigger.
For big gate-level designs, using Temporal Flow View (TFV) together with Data
Expansion is slower. Contact your local support for a workaround.
Individual Data Expansion setup for each FSDB is not supported. The DE setup
options for the different FSDB files have to be the same. For example, if the primary
FSDB used for the initial DE setup needs a mapping file, the same mapping file also
applies to the other FSDB files.
Siloti does not automatically detect whether the loaded FSDB is generated from a
different design or the same design. For now, try to avoid triggering DE associated
with a FSDB from a different design. For example, drag and drop a signal from
nTrace to nWave loaded with an FSDB associated with a different design.

Assertions
*

If Data Expansion is enabled in the time window mode (when the Specify Time
Window for Data Expansion option is on) and the time window is changed, the
Assertion Evaluator cannot evaluate the new time window. The recommendation
is to enable Data Expansion in the auto time window mode (AUTO Time Window
Mode option is on) while running the Assertion Evaluator.

Verilog Compiler for 2009
The Verdi Verilog compiler can parse some IEEE Standard 1800TM-2009 SystemVerilog
LRM constructs even when you do not specify the -2009 option. To parse an IEEE
Standard 1800TM-2009 SystemVerilog LRM design correctly, specify -2009 explicitly.
The following constructs can be parsed only with the -2009 option:
*

Local parameter in config section

config CC; localparam P = 3;

endconfig

Compiling Designs with Long Expressions
*

For designs containing very long expressions, statements, or similar constructs,
the compiler may error out with a segmentation fault due to the large number of OS
function calls involved. This problem can be avoided by first running the unlimit
command prior to executing the compiler.

VHDL Compiler
*

The VHDL compiler does not support a mix of VHDL-2008 and earlier versions
of VHDL design code. If your design contains a mix of VHDL- 2008 and earlier
versions, the entire design needs to be recompiled with the -vhdl08 option. If your
design does not contain any VHDL-2008 code, it does not need to be recompiled.

www.ieee.org are supported with the following known issues and limitations.

command in the Temporal Flow View.
Behavior Analysis does not support Verilog Event type signals.

Known Issues
*

Active trace and the assertion checker do not support tagged unions.
Performance may degrade for vericom or Import Design from the source with

work.

Clock trees cannot be extracted and displayed for interface signals.

Modport cannot be traversed in the nTrace source code window using the

*

Drag and drop of function arguments from the nTrace window into the

*

Use the following environment variable to work around this problem:

The result of using Watch Expression to display the SystemVerilog Assertion

When a stream name contains if, while, or forever, the created stream name in the

If the scope verificationTop.testComponent.aluChecker

SystemVerilog IEEE 1800-2005 syntax support is complete except for the following:
*

Nested modules and interfaces.
$root: Incremental compilation and multiple library import are not supported
Cannot find the mapping declaration for the loop-id of foreach statement.
Macro with an illegal identifier is not supported.

define IFQ_DAT_SRCINST<$cpu> <%61+$cpu%>
*

Interface extern function is not supported.
modport.function inside interface is not supported.
Implicit argument of modport is not supported.
Forward reference on coverage is not supported.

The nTrace source code view and static drive/load is supported except for the following:
*

(class) Inherited object, property/sequence
(class) parameterized class
(class) super and this
(package) property in package

The IEEE Standard 1800TM-2012 SystemVerilog LRM syntax is supported in the
nWave window except for the following:
*

Sliced tagged/packed unions (for example, tagged-union[3:2]) are not supported.
Masks cannot be drawn on sliced vectors.

When a value is entered for stable time in the Set Search Constraint form (invoked

When the Skip Bus Details option is turned on in the Toggle Coverage form

Trace into Function:
*

The statements in a function should be synthesizable. For example, the assert
statement inside a function is not supported.
The evaluation between an array and an integer is not supported. For example:

function mytype add_func(mytype data1,int i1); bit
[7:0][1:0] tmp1, tmp2;
tmp1 = data1[1] + i1; // array add integer. tmp2 =
data1[0] + i1;
add_func = {tmp1,tmp2}; endfunction

*

The type and number aggregations are not supported.
The argument index of external signal is not supported. For example:

function void func1 (int s); node [WIDTH-1:0]
j;
//find first for the first "one". U117H = 0;
FOREACH_I(WIDTH)
if (U111H[c[s].A]. y[j]) begin U117H = j; end
endfunction

FSDB Logging:
*

$fsdbLog is only supported in pure Verilog or mixed Verilog and SystemVerilog
designs.
There are up to a total of 1024 variables and strings allowed in one

$fsdbLog call.

*

Automatically assigned stream names add '\' to the first character of the stream
name if the full class instance name of the $fsdbLog contains a

special character. For example, top.\test.a.b.c .InstA. generates an automatic stream
name of "\top_\test.a.b.c _InstA".
*

There is a limit on the total number of variable attributes that can be dumped in an
FSDB file. Currently, the limit is 60000; the rest are ignored.
$psprintf is the only task which can be used as label, message, stream_name,
and variable in $fsdbLog.
$psprintf cannot be passed to label, message, stream, or string arguments if
ModelSim simulator is being used.

SystemVerilog Assertions Limitations
The following are the limitations of the SystemVerilog Assertions:
Assertion Evaluator
The following are not supported by the Assertion Evaluator feature:
* Immediate assert - not planned.
* Expect statements - not planned.
* Embedded concurrent assertions are partially supported. Clocks can be inferred, but
not the enabling condition.

* Nested enabled conditions whose nested level is >1.
* Sequences with built-in functions, matched, and triggered.
* Recursive properties and sequences.
* SVA system tasks with clock expression.
* Real type operand.
* Do not mix HDL designs and assertions in the same module. For this coding style, you
must dump the assertion module.
* Local variables are not saved to the FSDB by the assertion evaluator.
* The Verdi system parser supports the SVA extension syntax proposed by the IEEE
P1800 standard working group. The Assertion Evaluator does not support this syntax.
* Assertions inside functions.
Add Temporary Assertions
The following are not supported by the Add Temporary Assertions feature:
* Add temporary assertions feature does not support VHDL design.
* Macro Definition
SVA Binding
The following are not supported for the SVA Binding feature:
* Mixed with VHDL: Cannot bind with the absolute path signal in port instance. For
example:
bind CPU CHK ichk( .clk( top.ialu.clk) , );

* Both modes (pure and mixed): You cannot perform trace-drive-load from outside the
bound module.
Add Relevant Expression Node to nWave
The following is not supported for the "Add Relevant Expression Node to nWave" feature:
* An expression containing a function is not supported. For example:
a_s1 : assert property( @(clk) myfunc(a)==1 );

FSDB Dumper
This topic has the following sections:
* General Limitations
* Third-Party Simulator Limitations
* General Known Issues
* Clocking Blocks
* Assertions

General Limitations
*

New values of arrays passed to std::randomize() are not supported.
PSL and OVA languages are not supported.
Partial bit dumping is not supported.
Cannot dump immediate assertion syntax.
Cannot dump sequence and property.
Synopsys VCS Simulators:
Cannot dump SV dynamic constructs (for example, Class, Coverage, and
associate array) due to simulator API dependency.
Cannot dump PSL properties by adding the +psl_prop option in the

$fsdbDumpPSL FSDB dumping command.

Third-Party Simulator Limitations
The following are the FSDB dumper third-party simulator limitations:
* The dumping of the following signal types are not supported:
SV interface modport
Nettype
Power object

FSDB and Essential Signal Dumping

General Known Issues
*

Cannot use multiple dumpers (for example, HDL and HVL dumpers) in the parallel
mode simultaneously.
The usage of a colon (:) for the instance argument of the fsdbDumpvars task
generates an invalid argument error during simulation.

Clocking Blocks
Certain signal types (array, enum, struct, and union) inside clocking blocks are not dumped
into the FSDB file.

Assertions
*

The FSDB dumper uses a callback to get the Assertion KILL status because VCS
does not maintain the Assertion KILL status and the KILL statuses are grouped to
OFF status. When calling $assertkill after $assertoff, there will be no callback for
$assertkill.

Note for Using SKIP_CELL_INSTANCE
If the SKIP_CELL_INSTANCE environment variable is on and an essential signal is inside
a cell instance, then the output/inout ports of the cell instance is dumped. The essential
signals inside the cell instance are not dumped.

Tcl/Tk Interface
When xhost+ is executed, certain Tcl/Tk functions such as the send command are
affected and cannot work properly. Contact your Xserver vendor to prevent using the
xhost+ command.
It is recommended to use the xauth command instead of the xhost+ command to avoid
the send command issue and solve the DISPLAY issue.
For example, you can use the xauth command to display the authorization information
used in connecting to the X server as follows:
% env|grep DISPLAY
Output: DISPLAY=<DISPLAY NAME>
%## get authority string ##
% xauth list $DISPLAY
Output: <DISPLAY NAME PROTOCOL NAME HEX
KEY>

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
You can also use the xauth command to add an authorization entry for the indicated
display using the given protocol and key data as follows:
% setenv DISPLAY <DISPLAY NAME>
% novas
This command fails to invoke novas and displays the following message:

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
Xlib: connection to "<machine name>" refused by server Xlib: Client is
not authorized to connect to Server
invalidDisplay::xtInitialize::XtToolkitError::Can't open display:
<machine name>

title: Verification ContinuumTM
text:
%## set authority string ##
% xauth add <DISPLAY NAME PROTOCOL NAME HEX KEY>
% novas
This command invokes novas successfully

text:
Limitations of Behavior Analysis

Limitations of Behavior Analysis
In general, the Behavior Analysis engine black boxes non-synthesizable syntax. Examples
include a while loop and an always statement without a sensitivity list.
The following are known limitations of the Behavior Analysis engine:
* VHDL Unconstrained Signal
Consider the following example:
entity xxx is port (tttt: out std_logic_vector); end xxx;

The unconstrained signal, tttt, in the example is not supported.
* Verilog Streaming Operator
Consider the following example:
assign {>>{capi_din}} = a;

The streaming operator, {>>{capi_din}}, in the example is not supported.
The BA limitation messages are written to the haps.log file. The following examples show
typical log entries:
[BA] Warning:Unconstrained signal(IN1) is not supported.
[BA] Warning:Unconstrained signal(OUT1) is not supported.
[BA] Warning: Streaming operator (assign {>>{capi_din}} = a;
file=case_streamassign.sv,line=5) is not supported.

Limitations of Data Expansion
In general, the Data Expansion engine cannot calculate any signals that are driven by
black boxes and inferenced by the Behavior Analysis engine. The following are the known
limitations of the Data Expansion engine:
* The -sfile option of the sidExpandFsdbTCL does not support comments.
* In a HAPS flow, Data Expansion may use VHDL enum and VHDL integer inputs to
create a bus signal in a waveform. The exception to the creation of such signals are
enums with two states that are mapped to dumped signals.
