Transactions
SVTB-based testbench environments are typically built on an SVTB verification library/
methodology like OVM/UVM. Synopsys has leveraged the OVM/UVM infrastructure to
record component and port transactions flowing up and down the testbench into the FSDB
file. The Synopsys mechanism uses OVM/UVM transaction recording to capture testbench
transactions in the FSDB file for debug and analysis in the Verdi platform.

spreadsheet-like view.
transaction

The canvas view support enables visualizing, analyzing, and querying RTL objects in the

User Interface
You can open the canvas view in the following three ways:

Tcl Command
You can enable the canvas view and open its user interface using the following Tcl
schCreateCanvasWindow

You must specify the canvasType and scope arguments in the following command:
schCreateCanvasWindow -canvasType $type -valueType $valueType -scenario
$scenarioName -scope $scopeName

The command consists of the following arguments:
* -canvasType: Specify it as congestion or power.
* -valueType: The valueType argument depends on the canvasType. If the valueType
argument is not specified, by default metrics_cong_num_in_hot_spot is set for
congestion and total_power is set for power.
For congestion, you can specify the following arguments:
metrics_cong_num_in_hot_spot(default),
metrics_cong_cell_padding,
metrics_cong_logic_cong,
metrics_cong_overflow
For power, you can specify the following arguments:
total_power(default),
internal_power,
switching_power,
leakage_power,
glitch_power
* -scenario: You can use this argument only when the canvasType is Power. If it is not
specified, it uses the first scenario as the default value.
* -scope: Specify the scope module that you want to open.
schCreateCanvasWindow -canvasType power -scope top.cpu -valueType
total_power -scenario func.ss0p95v125c
schCreateCanvasWindow -canvasType congestion -scope top.cpu -valueType

Simprofile
The Simprofile feature in Verdi is used for profiling simulation performance. It allows you
to measure where the program spent its runtime and provides insights into the functions
called during execution. This profiling data is generated by VCS commands and stored
in a simprofile database. The profileView window in Verdi shows the CPU time of the
module, instance, and assertion.
This chapter contains the following sections:
* Loading the Simprofile Database (W-2024.09 and Earlier Releases)
* Loading the Simprofile Database (X-2025.06 Release Onward)
* Opening profileView
* profileView Window Panes
* Menus and Commands of the profileView Window
* Source View Indicator
* SVA Distribution Mode
* Merged Simprofile Report
* DUT/TB Proportion Display
* Limitations

Loading the Simprofile Database (W-2024.09 and Earlier Releases)

Loading the Simprofile Database (W-2024.09 and Earlier
Releases)
The profileView window uses the simprofile database generated by the VCS command
line. To load the database from the VCS command line, perform the following steps:
1. Run the following compile-time option in VCS:
%vcs -simprofile

2. Run the following runtime option in VCS:
%simv -simprofile time+json_dbg_field

3. Set the following environment variable:
setenv VERDI_SIMPROFILE_VIEW 1

4. Launch Verdi using the following command:
%verdi -apex -lca -profilePath <profile_database_path> -profileFilter
<percentage>

Where,
-profilePath <profile_database_path>: Specifies the path of the profile
database.
-profileFilter <percentage>: (Optional) Specifies the threshold percentage of
CPU time. The default value is 0.5 percent.
-lca: Enables the LCA feature.
-apex: Opens Verdi in Apex mode.

Loading the Simprofile Database (X-2025.06 Release Onward)
The profileView window uses the simprofile database generated by the VCS command
line. To load the database from the VCS command line, perform the following steps:
1. Run the following compile-time option in VCS:
%vcs -simprofile

2. Run the following runtime option in VCS:
%simv -simprofile time+json_dbg_field

Opening profileView

3. Launch Verdi using the following command:
%verdi -apex -profilePath <profile_database_path> -profileFilter
<percentage>

Where,
-profilePath <profile_database_path>: Specifies the path of the profile
database.
-profileFilter <percentage>: (Optional) Specifies the threshold percentage of
CPU time. The default value is 0.5 percent.
-apex: Opens Verdi in Apex mode.

The Detail pane provides in-depth information across seven tabs:

exception of the Summary tab, which remains static.

When you enable the Mark Profile Time option in the Preferences window of Verdi,
nTrace automatically marks the exclusive percentage before the line number in the

shown in Figure 470. The time on the line of module is equal to the exclusive module time
minus the total time of construct in the current module. The information disappears if the
window is closed.

you use the Marco folder, the entire Marco is displayed in the Source Code window.

Limitations of the Source View Indicator
The source view indicator has the following limitations:
* If the current instance used to navigate to the source code is filtered out in the

The Simprofile feature in Verdi has the following limitations:
* Does not support save session and restore session.
* Does not support cross-platforms. For example, Verdi_linux_64bit can correctly
load the profile database only from VCS_linux_64bit.
* Supports only time profiling. Memory profiling and performance analysis are not
supported.
* Supports only concurrent assertions; other assertion types are not supported.
* Supports only the post-simulation mode.
* Supports loading the profile database only from the consistent version and sub-version
of VCS. For example, Verdi_2016.06-1 can correctly load the profile database only
from VCS_2016.06-1.
* The functions or tasks in the Caller Callee tab are related only to the constructs in the
Construct tab.
* Supports only Verilog as the component filter.
* Supports showing only the top-N instance list.
* Does not support RMB context menus in the Summary and Filter panes of the
profileView window.
* Cannot identify if an object is addable in the RMB context menu.

* Does not support the Show in Detail RMB context menu in the Top N Usage pane.
You can double-click the pane instead to view the details.
* Does not support the Show in Source Code RMB context menu in the Detail pane.
You can double-click the pane instead to view the source code.

Appendix A: Supported Waveform Formats
This appendix covers the following topics:
* Fast Fourier Transformers (FFT)
* EVCD
* Analog Waveform Example

In addition to the FSDB waveform format, the following formats are supported:
* VCD (Value Change Dump)
* EVCD (Extended Value Change Dump)
* Analog - Powermill, Spice

Fast Fourier Transformers (FFT)
nWave provides the capability of viewing and analyzing analog signals in the frequency
domain. An FFT window in nWave is used to display and process frequency waveforms.
nWave can process analog signals through FFT to get the frequency results.

Getting Data From Analog Signal
After analog signals are imported into nWave, choose the Analog -> FFT command to
access the FFT window.

Fast Fourier Transformers (FFT)

Figure 480

Open FFT from nWave

The FFT window is created without any waveforms displayed.
Choose the Signal -> Add FFT Signal command in the FFT window.
The FFT Input Parameters form displays, as shown in the following figure. You can specify
parameters for FFT in this form.
Figure 481

Add FFT Signal Form

Fast Fourier Transformers (FFT)

Target signal can be specified through nWave window selection or drag from nWave into
the Signal Name text box. The Start and Stop times have to be specified to define the
range of the FFT process.
Stop

Seven types of window functions (rectangular, Blackman, Hamming, Hanning, Parzen,
Triangular and Welch) can be used in nWave. The resolution of the FFT result can be
specified with sample point number or sample rate.
Different FFT methods on the same target signal can be compared in the FFT window.
Select the signal in the FFT window, then use the Edit -> Calculate Selected command.
The different parameters are specified in the FFT Input Parameters [2] form (as shown in
the following figure), and the recalculated waveform are displayed for comparison.
Enable the Override option to overwrite the original result.
